entries.reason: Bash exit codes give a binary pass or fail that suits structural checks naturally.

entries.note: Giving agents a blocking content-quality signal in the fix loop is declined; non-blocking hygiene flags substitute.
entries.reason: Agents loop readily on printed errors but receive no signal for mediocre content.

entries.note: claude plugin eval exists; the eval suite adopts it to exercise a smoke run and grade output.
entries.reason: The plugin framework offered no built-in harness for scoring agent output during development.

entries.note: Hook and script conventions favoring deterministic validators are ecosystem norms.
entries.reason: Hook and script conventions steer plugin authors toward deterministic validators.

entries.note: hygiene.json flags redundant and restating reasons, complementing fragment error logs.
entries.reason: Run logs show fragment errors but never flag a boring or redundant reason.

entries.note: Stdlib token-overlap heuristics can flag duplicates and restatements without models; semantic judgment beyond that stays declined.
entries.reason: Judging reason quality needs a model or semantic comparison, which a dependency-free Python script cannot perform.

entries.note: Dropping the stdlib-only design to add quality dependencies is declined to keep zero-dependency offline install.
entries.reason: The script deliberately uses only the standard library to avoid install friction for plugin users.

entries.note: Users' pip or virtualenv availability is an environment fact outside plugin control.
entries.reason: Plugin users may lack pip access or a configured virtual environment.

entries.note: Claude Code plugin manifests lacking a dependency install step is a platform fact.
entries.reason: Claude Code plugins have no dependency installation step in their manifest.

entries.note: Embedding libraries are declined; stdlib heuristics in IMP-06 cover duplicate detection instead.
entries.reason: Embedding libraries would bloat a small plugin with heavy model downloads.

entries.note: Author's past Python environment conflicts are motivation only; stdlib-only stance is retained.
entries.reason: Past Python environment conflicts made the author wary of external packages.

entries.note: README documents stdlib-only as a deliberate design decision, including portability rationale.
entries.reason: Cross-platform portability is easiest to guarantee with pure standard-library code.

entries.note: Near-duplicate detection via stdlib token overlap discounting ancestor words catches many paraphrases without embeddings.
entries.reason: Detecting paraphrased duplicates requires embeddings or an LLM, not string equality.

entries.note: Token-overlap near-duplicate flags catch rephrasings that share key words, beyond exact matching.
entries.reason: Agents rephrase the same cause in different words, defeating exact matching.

entries.note: True semantic sameness needs embeddings or models, declined; surface token-overlap flags are the accepted limit.
entries.reason: Fuzzy ratios like difflib catch surface overlap but miss semantic sameness.

entries.note: Embedding APIs requiring keys and network calls are explicitly declined for the script.
entries.reason: Embedding APIs need keys and network access the script cannot assume.

entries.note: Flags are non-blocking annotations, so an imperfect threshold only mislabels, never deletes; no labeled data required.
entries.reason: Choosing a similarity threshold needs labeled data that does not exist yet.

entries.note: About 7.6M stdlib token-set comparisons is tractable; the hygiene report performs this whole-tree pass at assemble.
entries.reason: Pairwise comparison across 3,905 reasons means millions of comparisons, discouraging naive attempts.

entries.note: A model judge inside the check loop is declined for cost, latency and flakiness.
entries.reason: Calling a model inside the check step would add cost and latency to every retry loop.

entries.note: Per-retry model calls multiplying cost is exactly why an in-loop LLM judge is declined.
entries.reason: Each branch agent may retry several times, multiplying any per-check model call.

entries.note: Twenty-five parallel judging invocations are avoided by declining an LLM judge in the check step.
entries.reason: Twenty-five parallel branches would each trigger their own judging invocation.

entries.note: init --model lets users choose cheaper models instead of always inheriting an expensive default.
entries.reason: The default model is already expensive, so a second judging pass would roughly double spend.

entries.note: Check stays fast stdlib validation; slow model-based judging in the loop is declined.
entries.reason: Check commands must return quickly so agents do not stall mid-task.

entries.note: Nondeterministic judge verdicts causing flaky retries is the stated reason this remedy is declined.
entries.reason: A model judge is itself nondeterministic, making pass or fail flaky across retries.

entries.note: Assemble has the whole tree, so hygiene flags children restating a parent or any ancestor.
entries.reason: Judging whether a reason is a real cause rather than a restatement needs the ancestor chain.

entries.note: Restatement checks move to assemble, where problem and ancestor chain are available, instead of per-fragment check.
entries.reason: The check command receives only a fragment path, not the problem or ancestor reasons.

entries.note: Fragments need not carry the chain; the assembled tree provides ancestors for restatement flags.
entries.reason: Fragment files omit the parent chain, so off-topic detection has no reference point.

entries.note: Hygiene at assemble avoids redesigning the check CLI to accept context.
entries.reason: Passing context into check would need a richer CLI interface nobody designed.

entries.note: Judging genuine causality is interpretation, declined for the plugin; only mechanical restatement flags are allowed.
entries.reason: Causality is subjective and resists encoding as simple deterministic rules.

entries.note: Assemble-time hygiene compares children against ancestors written by other agents across fragments.
entries.reason: Restatement detection must compare against levels written earlier by a different agent.

entries.note: Hygiene report runs after all fragments exist, detecting cross-branch duplication the per-fragment check cannot.
entries.reason: Cross-branch duplication is only visible after all fragments exist, but check runs per fragment.

entries.note: Branch prompts list other level-1/level-2 reasons as covered elsewhere, giving isolated agents sibling awareness.
entries.reason: Each branch agent runs check before its siblings finish, so peers are not visible.

entries.note: Assemble gains a global hygiene pass writing hygiene.json with duplicate and near-duplicate flags.
entries.reason: The assemble step was built for merging, not for global deduplication analysis.

entries.note: Rejecting completed duplicates and re-dispatching is pruning, declined; flags annotate without deleting.
entries.reason: Rejecting duplicates after completion would require re-dispatching already finished agents.

entries.note: The shared level-1/level-2 digest in branch prompts partitions coverage among branches beforehand.
entries.reason: No orchestrator step exists to partition cause categories among branches beforehand.

entries.note: No keep-or-drop duplicate policy is needed: the plugin never prunes; the user decides.
entries.reason: Deciding which duplicate to keep needs a policy the design never specified.

entries.note: Principle clarification separates allowed mechanical aids from interpretation, so hygiene checks no longer seem forbidden.
entries.reason: The principle that analysis belongs to the user discouraged any automated judgment of reason content.

entries.note: Generating raw material rather than conclusions remains the user's requirement; plugin-side conclusions stay declined.
entries.reason: The author wanted the plugin to generate raw material, not impose conclusions on the user's thinking.

entries.note: Five Whys practice valuing human reasoning is a fact about the method itself.
entries.reason: Five Whys practice values the human's own reasoning over automated verdicts.

entries.note: Eager, shallow summarization by earlier AI tools is an ecosystem observation outside plugin control.
entries.reason: Earlier AI tools that summarized eagerly produced shallow, overconfident answers.

entries.note: Neutrality is preserved: the plugin does not rank or select causes.
entries.reason: A neutral generator avoids steering users toward causes the model happens to prefer.

entries.note: README records generation-only as a deliberate design decision keeping scope small and explainable.
entries.reason: Separating generation from analysis kept the plugin's scope small and easy to explain.

entries.note: Downstream reading gets explicit hygiene flags rather than relying on the reader to spot weak reasons unaided.
entries.reason: The author trusted in-context reading downstream to sort weak reasons from strong ones.

entries.note: Docs explicitly distinguish hygiene filtering aids from analysis, ending the conflation.
entries.reason: Filtering reasons was conflated with analyzing them, so quality gates seemed to violate the principle.

entries.note: Skill, agent and README now draw the line between hygiene checks and interpretive ranking.
entries.reason: No distinction was drawn between hygiene checks and interpretive ranking.

entries.note: Hygiene flags annotate only and never reject, so no reason's merit is judged.
entries.reason: Rejecting a reason feels like judging its merit, which the principle forbids.

entries.note: Agent and skill text will scope the no-ranking rule to interpretation, not mechanical checks.
entries.reason: Agent instructions forbid analyzing or ranking, and that taboo spread to the checker.

entries.note: Principle clarification defines which automated aids are acceptable and which stay with the user.
entries.reason: Design notes never defined which kinds of automated judgment are acceptable.

entries.note: Nothing is deleted: hygiene flags are annotations, so no genuine cause is silently discarded.
entries.reason: Fear of silently discarding a genuine cause made any filter look dangerous.

entries.note: Readers receive hygiene flags pointing at weak or duplicate reasons instead of catching them unaided.
entries.reason: The user was assumed to read the whole output in context and catch weak reasons there.

entries.note: Sizing rationale held: the measured output is about 128k tokens, fitting a 1M context.
entries.reason: The ~150k-token file was sized to fit whole into a 1M-token context window.

entries.note: Rather than assuming readers discount vacuous lines, hygiene flags mark duplicates and restatements explicitly.
entries.reason: Designers assumed a model reading the file would naturally discount vacuous lines.

entries.note: How well a model filters noise in context is a model capability; the plugin supplies hygiene flags instead.
entries.reason: Nobody tested whether in-context reading actually filters noise effectively.

entries.note: Trust in large context windows is an industry attitude outside plugin control.
entries.reason: Very large context windows invite trust that more material always helps analysis.

entries.note: Agent instructions demanding problem-specific reasons put quality responsibility back on the generator.
entries.reason: Pushing the burden downstream moved quality responsibility off the generator.

entries.note: Complete exhaustive trees are the user's requirement; dropping volume for precision is declined.
entries.reason: Exhaustive fan-out was chosen to maximize coverage, making volume the goal rather than precision.

entries.note: Parameterized breadth/depth lets users trade reason count for per-reason value while keeping trees complete.
entries.reason: A fixed 5x5 shape guarantees reason count but says nothing about value per reason.

entries.note: Redundant reasons are flagged as near-duplicates rather than silently counted as extra recall.
entries.reason: Coverage-first thinking treats redundant reasons as harmless extra recall.

entries.note: Honest README documents what validation covers and known limitations, countering thoroughness-by-count impressions.
entries.reason: An impressive total of 3,905 reasons made the output feel thorough by default.

entries.note: Pruning weak reasons breaks complete trees, which the user requires; declined.
entries.reason: Pruning weak reasons would break the uniform shape the assembler depends on.

entries.note: Hygiene counts of duplicates, restatements and over-length reasons give mechanical precision measures alongside coverage.
entries.reason: Precision metrics were never defined alongside the coverage target.

entries.note: Automated quality scoring is plugin-side judgment, declined; only mechanical hygiene flags are allowed.
entries.reason: Automated quality scoring would require opinionated criteria the author had not yet settled.

entries.note: A universal quality rubric for scoring is declined; domain judgment stays with the user.
entries.reason: Good root causes differ by domain, making a universal rubric hard to write.

entries.note: A specific-vs-generic example in agent instructions makes 'specific enough' concrete at generation time.
entries.reason: Deciding what counts as specific enough involves taste rather than rules.

entries.note: The first real run happened on 2026-09-13 and this catalog now settles the postponed decisions.
entries.reason: The author postponed contested design decisions until after a first real run.

entries.note: Gathering user feedback or research is a social remedy, not a plugin change.
entries.reason: No user feedback exists yet to reveal what users consider low quality.

entries.note: Caution about early criteria explains v0.1.0; the catalog commits only to mechanical, non-blocking flags.
entries.reason: Committing to criteria early risked locking in the wrong definition of value.

entries.note: Assemble now also emits content hygiene flags, so shape is no longer the only reported problem.
entries.reason: Assembly crashes on bad shape, while weak content still yields a complete file, so shape was the only blocker.

entries.note: Child count comes from breadth stored in run.json rather than a literal five.
entries.reason: The assembler expects exactly five children per node, so any count mismatch breaks ids.

entries.note: Fixed positional ids suit complete trees; variable fan-out that would break them is declined.
entries.reason: Dotted ids like 2.5.3.1 assume fixed child positions at every level.

entries.note: Plan, check and assemble read shape from run.json instead of hard-coded 5x5 constants.
entries.reason: The hard-coded 5x5 shape is baked into both the planner and the assembler.

entries.note: Variable fan-out is declined; every tree stays complete, so id generation stays simple.
entries.reason: Variable fan-out would complicate id generation and fragment file naming.

entries.note: Speed of writing simple positional code is past motivation; nothing further to change.
entries.reason: Simple positional code was faster to write than flexible tree handling.

entries.note: assemble --partial writes a valid tree with missing-branch markers instead of failing at seams.
entries.reason: Stitching branch fragments onto root nodes requires exact counts at the seam.

entries.note: Eval suite grades hygiene report presence, broadening success beyond producing a complete file.
entries.reason: Pipeline success was defined as producing a complete file, the easiest end-to-end signal to verify.

entries.note: Recorded per-level counts, words per level, bytes and tokens add measurable signals beyond a binary finished file.
entries.reason: A finished file is binary and demonstrable, unlike analytical usefulness.

entries.note: Pipeline-centric milestone framing is past process with nothing further to change.
entries.reason: Milestones were framed as the pipeline working rather than the output helping users.

entries.note: README includes a real excerpt, so demonstration shows actual output rather than mere completion.
entries.reason: Demonstrating a plugin only requires showing it runs to completion.

entries.note: Eval case states acceptance criteria: valid shape and a present hygiene report for a smoke run.
entries.reason: No acceptance test states what a good tree must contain.

entries.note: General engineering habit of runnable-first explains ordering; no artifact change.
entries.reason: Engineering habit prioritizes runnable software before tuning output quality.

entries.note: Hygiene now consumes reason text programmatically, so content defects produce flags instead of failing silently.
entries.reason: Content defects fail silently because nothing downstream consumes reason text programmatically.

entries.note: Hygiene tokenizes reason text for overlap and length checks, so reasons are no longer opaque.
entries.reason: Reasons are opaque strings to the script and are never parsed for meaning.

entries.note: Near-duplicate grouping exposes redundancy mechanically without ranking, which stays declined.
entries.reason: No downstream step clusters or ranks reasons, which would expose redundancy.

entries.note: Soliciting quality reports from readers is a social feedback remedy, not a plugin change.
entries.reason: Output goes to a reader who rarely reports quality issues back to the author.

entries.note: A telemetry backend recording useful reasons is heavy infrastructure, declined.
entries.reason: No telemetry records which reasons users actually found useful.

entries.note: Distinguishing insightful from vacuous reasons is interpretation left to the user.
entries.reason: A vacuous sentence and an insightful one have identical JSON types.

entries.note: Quality-based retries in the fix loop are declined because they may never converge.
entries.reason: Retrying on shape is cheap and deterministic, while retrying on quality may never converge.

entries.note: Retrying for quality is declined since agents may repeat weak reasons; no quality gate in the loop.
entries.reason: An agent can always fix a bracket but may repeat the same weak reason on retry.

entries.note: Agents cap their fix loop and reply FAILED, giving every retry a stopping rule.
entries.reason: Quality retries have no natural stopping rule and risk endless loops.

entries.note: The deterministic check is kept; adding nondeterministic judging to it is declined.
entries.reason: Deterministic checks keep agent behavior predictable for the orchestrating skill.

entries.note: Self-critique rewriting wording without substance is a model behavior outside plugin control.
entries.reason: Model self-critique often rewrites wording without improving the underlying substance.

entries.note: Targeted Edit repairs replace full rewrites, conserving each branch agent's token budget.
entries.reason: Token budgets per branch agent limit how many full rewrites are affordable.

entries.note: README states what validation does and does not cover, making the data-contract scope explicit.
entries.reason: Fragment validation was designed as a data contract between agents and script, not as a review.

entries.note: Contracts specifying types rather than semantics is a general software convention.
entries.reason: Software contracts conventionally specify types and structure, not semantics.

entries.note: API-development JSON-schema habits explain the check's style; nothing further to change.
entries.reason: The check mirrors JSON-schema habits carried over from API development.

entries.note: Decoupled agents and script needing only a data interface is sound design history; no change implied.
entries.reason: Agents and script are decoupled components that only needed a data interface.

entries.note: Scarcity of semantic-contract patterns for LLM agents is an ecosystem fact.
entries.reason: Few established patterns exist for semantic contracts between LLM agents.

entries.note: Principle clarification documents that mechanical aids are allowed while judgment stays outside, with the user.
entries.reason: Separation of concerns placed judgment deliberately outside the interface boundary.

entries.note: Hygiene defines concrete testable criteria: exact and near-duplicates, ancestor restatements, over-length reasons.
entries.reason: No rubric defining a good reason existed, so there was nothing concrete for a checker to test.

entries.note: The Five Whys method's lack of formal validity criteria is a fact about the method.
entries.reason: The Five Whys method itself gives little formal guidance on what makes a valid why.

entries.note: Toyota shop-floor origins and facilitator reliance are historical method facts.
entries.reason: Classic Five Whys grew from Toyota shop floors and relies on facilitator judgment.

entries.note: Informal spread of the method without a codified standard is outside plugin control.
entries.reason: The method spread through informal training rather than a codified standard with criteria.

entries.note: Literature focusing on single causal chains is an ecosystem fact.
entries.reason: Most literature describes a single causal chain, not a 3,905-node branching tree.

entries.note: Agents state explicit assumptions, exposing unevidenced premises; verifying evidence stays with the user.
entries.reason: In practice validity rests on evidence, which generated reasons never carry.

entries.note: Rewritten agent instructions make tacit norms explicit: grounding, stated assumptions, specific-vs-generic example.
entries.reason: Adapting a human workshop technique to agents left its tacit norms unwritten.

entries.note: Measurable properties (duplicates, restatement, length) are checked mechanically in the hygiene report.
entries.reason: Agent instructions express quality as prose guidelines rather than measurable properties.

entries.note: Distinctness gets a numeric token-overlap threshold via near-duplicate and restatement flags.
entries.reason: Rules like distinct and concrete have no numeric thresholds attached.

entries.note: Writing prose guidance quickly is past process; testable criteria now come from IMP-06.
entries.reason: Prose guidance was faster to write than testable acceptance criteria.

entries.note: Over-length reasons are flagged in hygiene.json, so the 20-word rule is finally checked.
entries.reason: The roughly 20-word limit is the only quantified rule, and it goes unchecked.

entries.note: Instructions written for steering explains the gap; verifiable criteria now live in IMP-06.
entries.reason: Instructions were tuned to steer model behavior, not to enable script verification.

entries.note: Guidelines on distinctness, restatement and length are translated into mechanical hygiene checks.
entries.reason: Nobody translated the guidelines into a checklist a validator could apply.

entries.note: Agent instructions add a specific-vs-generic example anchoring good and bad reasons.
entries.reason: No labeled examples of good and bad reasons were collected to anchor a rubric.

entries.note: The 2026-09-13 full run produced a 3,905-reason corpus, kept in docs/self-improvement.
entries.reason: Without a full real run, no corpus of plugin output exists to label.

entries.note: Hand-labeling datasets is a human data-building effort, not a plugin change.
entries.reason: Hand-labeling thousands of reasons is tedious work for one person.

entries.note: An evals/ case for claude plugin eval brings evaluation into scope.
entries.reason: No evaluation dataset was included in the v0.1.0 scope.

entries.note: Scarcity of machine-readable public Five Whys examples is an ecosystem fact.
entries.reason: Public Five Whys examples are scarce and not machine-readable.

entries.note: Grading against gold-standard causes is plugin-side judgment; evals grade shape and hygiene only.
entries.reason: Gold-standard causes for arbitrary problems are inherently debatable.

entries.note: A stdlib unittest suite makes shape, plan, check, assemble and hygiene expectations executable.
entries.reason: The project has no tests or evals, so quality expectations were never made executable.

entries.note: Plugin culture rarely using eval suites is an ecosystem norm outside plugin control.
entries.reason: Plugin development culture rarely includes eval suites for prompt outputs.

entries.note: LLM output testing being less familiar than unit testing is an industry fact.
entries.reason: Testing LLM output is less familiar than unit testing deterministic code.

entries.note: A single smoke-preset eval case via existing claude plugin eval tooling keeps the harness lightweight.
entries.reason: Building an eval harness felt heavier than building the plugin itself.

entries.note: The eval suite adopts claude plugin eval directly.
entries.reason: Available plugin eval tooling was not adopted during the initial build.

entries.note: Evals assert shape validity and hygiene report presence, not exact text, sidestepping nondeterminism.
entries.reason: Nondeterministic model output makes exact pass or fail assertions awkward to write.

entries.note: Optional context intake grounds every prompt in the user's specifics instead of needing a generic rubric.
entries.reason: Reason value depends on the user's problem, so a generic rubric seemed unattainable up front.

entries.note: Generic cause-kind checklist is replaced with grounding in each problem's specifics, fitting reasons to the domain.
entries.reason: A cause insightful for software bugs may be useless for a business process problem.

entries.note: When a free-text problem is thin, the skill asks once for key specifics stored in run.json.
entries.reason: The plugin accepts any free-text problem, maximizing variation in what counts as good.

entries.note: Directly addressed: the skill asks for key specifics when the problem statement lacks detail.
entries.reason: Users often supply little problem detail, so relevance cannot be measured against specifics.

entries.note: Recognizing true root causes remains the user's analysis; the plugin does not select them.
entries.reason: Domain experts, not scripts, are usually the ones who recognize a true root cause.

entries.note: Per-run context intake provides domain tailoring now, without waiting for usage patterns.
entries.reason: The author deferred domain-specific tailoring until real usage revealed patterns.

entries.note: Sibling-aware branch prompts list the other level-1/2 reasons as covered elsewhere, reducing cross-branch repetition.
entries.reason: Branch agents run in isolation, so each cannot see what siblings produced and likely repeats causes.

entries.note: Directly addressed: branch prompts gain the level-1/2 digest in addition to their own ancestor chain.
entries.reason: Each branch prompt carries only its own ancestor chain, never reasons generated in other branches.

entries.note: Branch prompts can include the level-1/2 reasons, which exist before any branch launches, so simultaneity no longer means zero sibling awareness.
entries.reason: All branch agents launch simultaneously, so no sibling output exists when each prompt is generated.

entries.note: The skill now dispatches at most 20 agents per message: root first, then branches in rounds of 20 and 5.
entries.reason: The skill dispatches all 25 agents in one parallel batch to minimize wall-clock time.

entries.note: Author's prototyping impatience with sequential runs; parallelism stays, and IMP-07 adds coherence without serializing.
entries.reason: Sequential runs lasting many minutes felt unacceptable to the author during early prototyping.

entries.note: How Claude Code's Agent tool handles batched calls is platform behavior the plugin cannot change.
entries.reason: Claude Code's agent tool rewards batching many agent calls into a single message.

entries.note: Recording created-to-assembled duration gives a measured basis for weighing speed; the real run took about 7 minutes.
entries.reason: No latency budget was defined that could weigh speed against cross-branch coherence.

entries.note: Assumption about user patience; the measured full run took about 7 minutes, and nothing further follows.
entries.reason: The author assumed users would abandon a run that took over ten minutes.

entries.note: Feature-positioning motivation; parallel fan-out is retained and sibling context arrives without slowing it.
entries.reason: Parallel fan-out was the plugin's headline feature, so slowing it felt like a regression.

entries.note: Up-front generation from the root fragment is sufficient: the level-1/2 digest is available there for sibling-aware prompts.
entries.reason: The plan command generates every branch prompt up front from the level-2 fragment alone.

entries.note: Reproducibility rationale for plan; IMP-07 keeps plan a pure function of the root fragment.
entries.reason: Plan was designed as a pure function of the root fragment for easy reproducibility.

entries.note: Plan is re-run every round and already derives progress from fragments on disk, skipping valid ones.
entries.reason: Regenerating prompts mid-run would require the script to track partial progress state.

entries.note: Plan will group tasks into waves no larger than the concurrency cap for wave-by-wave dispatch.
entries.reason: The script has no notion of dispatch waves or staged prompt generation.

entries.note: Simplicity rationale for up-front planning; nothing further to change since IMP-07 preserves it.
entries.reason: Up-front planning made the check-and-assemble flow simpler to reason about.

entries.note: Making later prompts depend on earlier branch output serializes the run and is declined.
entries.reason: Nobody specified that later prompts could depend on earlier branch output.

entries.note: Seeding later waves with earlier branch output is declined; IMP-07 shares the cheap level-1/2 digest instead.
entries.reason: No staged wave design exists where early branches seed the prompts of later ones.

entries.note: Arbitrary priority among level-2 nodes is one reason seeded sequential waves are declined.
entries.reason: Wave ordering would force an arbitrary priority among the 25 level-2 nodes.

entries.note: Order-dependent bias is a cost of seeded waves, which the catalog declines.
entries.reason: Later waves would inherit bias from whichever branches happened to run first.

entries.note: Wave size becomes the concurrency cap (default 20), a mechanical choice needing no quality trade-off evidence.
entries.reason: Choosing wave sizes required evidence about trade-offs that nobody had gathered.

entries.note: Describes v0.1.0 scoping; orchestration additions are now covered by IMP-03 and IMP-07.
entries.reason: The v0.1.0 scope deliberately excluded orchestration beyond a single fan-out.

entries.note: Influence of prior art on the original design; no further artifact change follows.
entries.reason: Prior art the author referenced used flat map-reduce without iterative seeding.

entries.note: Subagents lacking peer messaging or shared scratchpads during execution is a Claude Code platform property.
entries.reason: Sub-agents cannot message each other or read a shared scratchpad during execution.

entries.note: Absence of peer-to-peer subagent messaging is a Claude Code limitation outside the plugin.
entries.reason: Claude Code sub-agents have no built-in peer-to-peer messaging channel.

entries.note: Shared scratchpad files across concurrent writers are declined; the level-1/2 digest is shared read-only via prompts.
entries.reason: A shared file would introduce race conditions across 25 concurrent writers.

entries.note: Own-fragment-only writing stays; shared state between agents is declined.
entries.reason: Agents are told to write only their own fragment, forbidding shared state.

entries.note: Polling shared files is part of the declined shared-scratchpad approach.
entries.reason: Polling a shared file would cost extra tokens and turns in every agent.

entries.note: Intentional subagent isolation is a platform design decision outside the plugin's control.
entries.reason: The platform isolates sub-agents intentionally to keep runs predictable and independent.

entries.note: Exposing in-progress fragments to siblings would be a shared scratchpad, which is declined.
entries.reason: Each agent writes its whole fragment in one final Write call, exposing nothing earlier.

entries.note: Rationale for single-fragment validation; check still validates complete fragments, nothing further needed.
entries.reason: Single-write output was chosen so the check command validates one complete tree.

entries.note: Valid reason incremental writes were avoided; no artifact change follows from it.
entries.reason: Incremental writes would leave half-formed JSON that fails shape validation.

entries.note: Streaming partial reasons to other branches is a form of cross-branch feeding the catalog declines.
entries.reason: Streaming partial reasons outward was never considered as an intermediate artifact.

entries.note: That model reasoning is internal until a tool call is a property of the model and platform.
entries.reason: Agents reason internally before writing, so intermediate state is never externally visible.

entries.note: Agent instructions will add outline-before-write and targeted Edit repairs instead of one mandated whole-file Write.
entries.reason: Instructions discouraging extra tool calls push agents toward one final write.

entries.note: Only the small level-1/2 digest is shared, not other branches' deep reasons, avoiding thousands of extra tokens.
entries.reason: Including other branches' reasons would bloat each prompt with thousands of extra tokens.

entries.note: Sharing just the 30 level-1/2 reasons keeps prompts small regardless of how many deep reasons exist.
entries.reason: Other branches together hold thousands of reasons, far beyond a useful prompt size.

entries.note: Geometric growth affects deep levels only; the shared level-1/2 digest stays constant in size.
entries.reason: The five-way fan-out multiplies content geometrically with every level added.

entries.note: The level-1/2 reasons serve as the compact shareable form, with no summarization needed.
entries.reason: Line-per-reason output has no compressed summary form that could be shared instead.

entries.note: A deduplicated cause catalog is synthesis and pruning; IMP-06 flags duplicates without merging anything.
entries.reason: No deduplicated cause catalog is produced that would be smaller than raw output.

entries.note: init --breadth/--depth makes the shape configurable, allowing smaller trees.
entries.reason: The hard-coded shape offers no smaller configuration to reduce cross-branch volume.

entries.note: Init and plan will report measured token estimates, making prompt-size costs visible.
entries.reason: The author never measured how many tokens a shared-context prompt would actually need.

entries.note: Per-agent input cost is why only a cheap level-1/2 digest is added, not full sibling output.
entries.reason: Prompt input is paid 25 times, so any added context scales run cost linearly.

entries.note: init --model lets users pick a cheaper model instead of inheriting the default.
entries.reason: Default-model pricing makes per-agent input tokens a visible cost driver.

entries.note: Prompt-cache engineering is declined as heavy infrastructure.
entries.reason: No prompt caching strategy was designed around a shared common prefix.

entries.note: Past prioritization of cost over quality; quality work now proceeds via IMP-06/07/08.
entries.reason: The author optimized for low per-run cost before output quality was proven.

entries.note: The plugin computes no cost estimates at all today; IMP-05 would add run-level previews.
entries.reason: Cost estimates were computed per fragment, hiding cross-branch trade-offs.

entries.note: A cost and size preview with confirmation lets cost-sensitive users decide before a full run.
entries.reason: Users on metered plans were assumed to be highly cost sensitive.

entries.note: A small, clearly labeled covered-elsewhere section limits dilution compared with full sibling output.
entries.reason: Long context was expected to dilute each agent's focus on its own node.

entries.note: Supplements abstract rules with a demonstrated specific-vs-generic example.
entries.reason: The agent definition relies on abstract rules instead of demonstrated quality.

entries.note: A model-driven critique-and-regenerate pass is declined as costly and flaky; non-blocking hygiene flags instead.
entries.reason: No second pass refines or regenerates weak leaves after the first draft.

entries.note: A critique-and-revise agent loop is the declined model-judge approach; hygiene flags substitute.

entries.note: Recorded tokens, bytes and duration per run replace unmeasured cost assumptions.

entries.reason: The output is a ~150k-token file too costly to produce and too large to read and use well.

entries.reason: The design requires exactly five reasons under every node, never allowing fewer where genuine causes run out.

entries.reason: The Python validator hard-codes the 5x5 shape and rejects any list not exactly five long.

entries.note: Hygiene report adds mechanical content checks (duplicates, restatements, length) beyond the easy structural validation.
entries.reason: Structure was checked because it is easy to verify mechanically, unlike content quality.

entries.reason: Variable-length lists would complicate the assembly and dotted id-numbering logic.

entries.note: init --breadth exposes the branching factor as a stored run parameter.
entries.reason: No configuration parameter for branching factor was exposed in v0.1.0.

entries.note: Predictable totals remain a deliberate benefit; nothing further to change beyond cost preview already in IMP-05.

entries.note: Prototype ordering explains v0.1.0; the real run happened 2026-09-13 and shape becomes configurable under IMP-01.
entries.reason: Early prototyping locked in the shape before any real run tested whether it fit.

entries.note: Exactly-five prompt instructions keep trees complete; relaxing counts is the declined variable fan-out remedy.
entries.reason: The generated prompts tell agents every whys list must contain exactly five items.

entries.note: Prompts and validator will both read the stored run shape rather than module literals.
entries.reason: Prompt templates are generated from the same fixed constants the validator uses.

entries.note: Padding with weak reasons is countered by specificity instructions, stated assumptions and specific-vs-generic examples.
entries.reason: Agents obey count instructions literally and pad with weak reasons rather than stop.

entries.note: Terminal or no-further-cause markers are declined 'not applicable' slots; every tree stays complete.
entries.reason: No instruction permits declaring "no further cause" or marking a branch terminal.

entries.note: Author's past fear of shallow answers explains fixed counts; no artifact change follows from the motivation itself.
entries.reason: The author feared variable counts would let agents return one or two shallow reasons.

entries.note: Letting agents judge causal saturation means stopping early, which the complete-tree requirement declines.
entries.reason: Prompt wording prioritizes format compliance over judgment about causal saturation.

entries.note: Breadth becomes an init parameter defaulting to 5, so symmetry is a default rather than a lock.
entries.reason: Five-by-five symmetry was chosen as an aesthetic echo of the Five Whys name.

entries.note: Parameterized shape turns the second five into a tunable breadth stored in run.json.
entries.reason: The "five whys, five reasons" concept was treated as a feature rather than a tunable parameter.

entries.note: Describability motivated the original shape; IMP-01 keeps 5x5 as a documented default.
entries.reason: A memorable, clean shape is easier to describe in a README and plugin description.

entries.note: README design-decisions section will state the basis for default breadth and how to change it.
entries.reason: Nobody challenged whether the second "five" had any methodological basis.

entries.note: Classic Five Whys defining depth only is a methodology fact outside the plugin's control.
entries.reason: Classic Five Whys specifies depth only, leaving breadth to be invented ad hoc.

entries.note: This self-review is the revisit; parameterization is covered by IMP-01.
entries.reason: The neat symmetry made the design feel complete and discouraged revisiting it.

entries.note: Users can pick a breadth matching their problem rather than inheriting the five-factor assumption.
entries.reason: The author assumed every cause naturally has about five contributing factors worth listing.

entries.note: Fishbone-inspired round number is design history; nothing further actionable beyond IMP-01.
entries.reason: Fishbone-style brainstorming suggests several cause categories, encouraging a round number.

entries.note: Sampling real root-cause analyses to measure branching is research or dataset building, not a plugin change.
entries.reason: No sample of real root-cause analyses was examined to measure typical branching.

entries.note: Models' ability to always generate five plausible reasons is a model property the plugin cannot change.

entries.note: Hygiene flags for near-duplicates and parent restatements surface padded reasons that shape checks miss.
entries.reason: Only shape checks exist, so padded or forced reasons were never noticed.

entries.note: Convenience for task sizing explains the assumption; no further artifact change follows.
entries.reason: The assumption was convenient because it simplified sizing of parallel tasks.

entries.note: Non-uniform branching per node is the declined adaptive fan-out; trees stay complete and uniform.
entries.reason: The parallel fan-out plan depends on uniform branching to split work into equal sub-agent tasks.

entries.note: Identical subtree sizes follow from complete trees, which remain required; ragged branches are declined.
entries.reason: Twenty-five branch agents each producing 155 reasons requires identical subtree sizes.

entries.note: Content-dependent planning implies adaptive fan-out or early stopping, declined for complete trees.
entries.reason: The orchestration plan is computed statically before any content is generated.

entries.note: A multi-round coordinator feeding generated content forward serializes the run and is declined.
entries.reason: Content-dependent dispatch would need a multi-round coordinator the script lacks.

entries.note: Merge and filename simplicity explain uniform tasks; nothing actionable remains.
entries.reason: Equal task sizes simplify merge ordering and fragment filename conventions.

entries.note: The skill already dispatches iteratively: root round, then capped branch rounds re-planned until ready.
entries.reason: Claude Code sub-agent dispatch favors one planned batch over iterative adaptive spawning.

entries.note: Pruning weak or irrelevant branches is plugin-side judgment reserved to the user; hygiene flags annotate instead.
entries.reason: Every reason at every level is expanded, with no pruning of weak, duplicate, or irrelevant branches.

entries.note: Scoring or ranking reasons before expansion is declined plugin-side analysis.
entries.reason: No step scores or ranks reasons before deciding which ones deserve further expansion.

entries.note: Principle clarification states which mechanical aids are allowed while branch importance stays with the user.
entries.reason: The plugin deliberately leaves all analysis, including branch importance, to the user.

entries.note: An extra scoring pass implies plugin-side ranking, which is declined regardless of cost.
entries.reason: Scoring would require an extra agent pass that adds cost and design complexity.

entries.note: A plausibility or relevance rubric exists only to rank reasons, a declined remedy.
entries.reason: No rubric for causal plausibility or relevance was defined to drive ranking.

entries.note: Relaxing the no-ranking instruction would move analysis into agents, which the catalog declines.
entries.reason: Agent instructions explicitly forbid analyzing, summarizing, or ranking reasons.

entries.note: Concern about biasing users explains the no-ranking rule; R-01 already records the decision.
entries.reason: The author worried model-driven ranking would bias users toward the model's opinions.

entries.note: Sibling-aware branch prompts list other level-1/2 reasons so isolated agents avoid duplicating them.
entries.reason: Branches expand in isolation, so no agent can spot duplicates that could be pruned.

entries.note: Branch prompts will include the level-1/level-2 digest beyond the agent's own ancestor chain.
entries.reason: Each branch agent receives only its own ancestor chain, never other branches' output.

entries.note: The cheap level-1/2 digest restores some cross-branch awareness without giving up parallel speed.
entries.reason: Parallel dispatch trades cross-branch awareness for wall-clock speed.

entries.note: Sharing full sibling fragments is the declined shared-output approach; IMP-07 shares only the small digest.
entries.reason: Sharing all sibling fragments would bloat every prompt and defeat the fan-out.

entries.note: assemble writes hygiene.json flagging exact and near duplicates, annotating without deleting.
entries.reason: The Python assembler has no post-generation deduplication pass.

entries.reason: Semantic duplicate detection needs embeddings or model calls the script avoids.

entries.note: Smoke preset and plan --only let users see a small tree or chosen branches before committing.
entries.reason: The workflow is single-pass, generating the whole tree before the user sees any of it.

entries.note: plan --only enables staged dispatch of selected branches instead of one all-at-once command.
entries.reason: The skill runs as one command rather than an interactive level-by-level session.

entries.note: After the root fragment, users can dispatch chosen branches via --only while each wave stays parallel.
entries.reason: Pausing for user choices between levels conflicts with unattended parallel execution.

entries.note: Preference for a finished artifact is past design motivation; staged options are covered by IMP-02.
entries.reason: The author optimized for a finished artifact over a guided exploration.

entries.note: Runs persist on disk: run.json plus fragments, and plan skips valid fragments, so partial trees can wait and resume.
entries.reason: No saved state lets a partial tree wait for user direction.

entries.note: Reliability of multi-turn checkpoints inside skills is a Claude Code platform characteristic.
entries.reason: Multi-turn checkpoints are awkward to encode reliably inside a Claude Code skill.

entries.note: Exhaustiveness is the user's stated requirement, not mere positioning; no further change follows.
entries.reason: Exhaustiveness was treated as the product's differentiator against ordinary chat-based Five Whys.

entries.note: Chat producing a free linear why chain is an ecosystem fact outside the plugin.
entries.reason: A normal chat conversation already produces one linear why chain for free.

entries.note: Need to justify existence is past motivation; the exhaustive tree is the user's requirement.
entries.reason: The plugin needed a visible reason to exist beyond what a single prompt could do.

entries.note: Honest README documents measured cost, time and limitations rather than headline reason counts.
entries.reason: Large reason counts look impressive and are easy to quantify in a description.

entries.note: Documentation will state what the tree is and is not, including known limitations, avoiding breadth-as-insight claims.
entries.reason: Breadth of output was confused with depth of insight when positioning the tool.

entries.note: User research on structured Five Whys needs is a social remedy, not a plugin change.
entries.reason: No user research established what people actually want from structured Five Whys.

entries.note: A root-cause stopping criterion implies early stopping or variable depth, declined for complete trees.
entries.reason: There is no stopping criterion for reaching a root cause or an actionable leaf.

entries.note: Principle clarification explicitly assigns root-cause judgment to the user and explains allowed mechanical aids.
entries.reason: Judging when a root cause is reached was delegated entirely to the user.

entries.note: README will document what shape validation covers and does not, including semantic conditions.
entries.reason: Shape validation cannot express semantic conditions like actionability or saturation.

entries.note: A terminal or out-of-scope field is the declined 'not applicable' slot.
entries.reason: The fragment format has no field for marking a reason terminal or out of scope.

entries.note: Early termination producing ragged trees is exactly the declined remedy; complete trees remain required.
entries.reason: Early termination would produce ragged trees that fail the fixed-count check.

entries.note: Per-branch stop-when-fixable means variable depth, declined; run-level depth choice comes via IMP-01.
entries.reason: The traditional "stop when fixable" heuristic was dropped in favor of fixed depth.

entries.note: init --depth lets each run choose depth, defaulting to five.
entries.reason: Depth is fixed at five by the technique's name rather than chosen to fit each problem.

entries.note: Depth becomes a stored run parameter so identity no longer forces five levels.
entries.reason: The tool's identity commits it to exactly five levels regardless of problem complexity.

entries.note: Defaults stay 5/5, preserving the recognizable brand while permitting other depths.
entries.reason: Parameterizing depth would seem to dilute the recognizable Five Whys brand.

entries.note: Popular summaries treating five as a rule are ecosystem culture outside the plugin's control.
entries.reason: Popular summaries of Toyota's method present five as a rule rather than a rule of thumb.

entries.note: Faithful-implementation scoping is past motivation; configurability is covered by IMP-01.
entries.reason: The plugin was scoped as a faithful implementation of a named technique.

entries.note: A --depth option lets simple problems use two or three levels.
entries.reason: Nobody asked whether simple problems reach root causes in two or three levels.

entries.note: Naming preceded usage data; the real run now supplies data and IMP-01 relaxes the lock.
entries.reason: Naming decisions were made before any usage data could inform them.

entries.note: init --depth overrides the module constant; plan, check and assemble read the stored shape.
entries.reason: Depth is a hard-coded constant in the script with no command-line override.

entries.note: MVP deferral explains the missing option; the configuration itself is IMP-01.
entries.reason: v0.1.0 was built as a minimum viable version with configuration deferred.

entries.note: Root/branch split will be derived from the stored depth instead of hard-wired levels 1-2 and 3-5.
entries.reason: The root-versus-branch split of levels 1-2 and 3-5 is hard-wired into planning logic.

entries.note: Parameterized shape includes computing agent partitioning from stored breadth and depth.
entries.reason: A depth flag would require recomputing agent partitioning dynamically.

entries.note: A stdlib unittest suite covering shapes, plan, check and assemble makes parameter changes safe.
entries.reason: No tests exist that would make parameter changes safe to attempt.

entries.note: Absence of requests is past context; this self-review motivates IMP-01.
entries.reason: No users had yet requested shallower trees to prompt the change.

entries.note: Users can shrink either breadth or depth per run, taming the multiplicative product while keeping trees complete.
entries.reason: Breadth and depth were combined multiplicatively, whereas classic Five Whys follows a single chain.

entries.note: Cost and size preview makes the combined breadth-times-depth cost explicit before dispatch.
entries.reason: Fishbone-style breadth was merged with Five Whys depth without reconciling their costs.

entries.note: Concern about single chains missing alternatives is a valid past rationale; nothing further to change.
entries.reason: Single-chain Five Whys was seen as prone to missing alternative causes.

entries.note: init and plan will report reason count and token estimates so context-limit consequences are visible.
entries.reason: The five-to-the-fifth combinatorial consequence was not weighed against context limits.

entries.note: Preview reports whole-tree totals, supplementing per-node rules with aggregate agent, reason and token counts.
entries.reason: Design reasoning happened in per-node rules rather than whole-tree totals.

entries.note: Lack of precedent for combined breadth-depth bounds is a field-wide fact.
entries.reason: No precedent existed showing sensible bounds for combined breadth and depth.

entries.note: Users doubting deeper levels' value can choose a shallower depth per run.
entries.reason: Each added level was assumed to add proportional insight rather than diminishing returns.

entries.note: Measuring level usefulness requires user studies or benchmark datasets, not a plugin change.
entries.reason: No evaluation measured whether level-5 reasons are more useful than level-3 reasons.

entries.note: Intuition that deeper feels more fundamental is past design psychology; depth choice is IMP-01.
entries.reason: Deeper causes intuitively feel more fundamental, biasing designers toward more depth.

entries.note: Hygiene flags for ancestor restatements and near-duplicates make depth-related quality decay mechanically visible.
entries.reason: Quality decay at depth was predicted but never tested before release.

entries.note: Per-level counts, average words and token approximations recorded in output expose per-level cost.
entries.reason: Per-level cost stays hidden because agents run in parallel out of the user's view.

entries.note: init --model with documented trade-offs lets users factor model pricing into runs.
entries.reason: Default-model pricing was not factored into estimates of each level's value.

entries.note: Keeping uniform depth is required; variable-depth branches are the declined remedy.

entries.note: Partial assembly writes explicit missing-branch markers, keeping dotted ids valid when subtrees are absent.
entries.reason: Dotted ids like 4.1.3.2.5 assume a complete tree to stay contiguous.

entries.note: assemble --partial handles missing subtrees with markers instead of refusing.
entries.reason: The assembler concatenates fragments by position rather than handling missing subtrees.

entries.reason: The output was designed for whole-file reading into context, favoring regularity over compactness.

entries.note: Intentional-end metadata exists only for ragged trees, which are declined.
entries.reason: Ragged trees would need extra metadata showing where a branch intentionally ended.

entries.note: NEW reconciled: keeping depth key and indentation for windowed reading; saving is small.
entries.reason: Implementation simplicity was prioritized over output economy for the first release.

entries.note: Following only probable chains requires plugin-side ranking and pruning, declined in favor of user analysis.
entries.reason: The author equated thoroughness with exhaustive coverage instead of following only the most probable causal chains.

entries.note: Fear of missing the root cause is past motivation aligned with the user's exhaustive requirement.
entries.reason: Fear of missing the true root cause pushed toward listing every plausible alternative.

entries.note: Confirmation-bias criticism of single-chain analysis is a methodology literature fact.
entries.reason: Single-chain analyses are criticized for confirmation bias toward the first plausible cause.

entries.note: A confidence signal to drop causes is plugin-side ranking and pruning, declined.

entries.note: Completeness as defense against 'shallow' is past psychology; nothing further actionable.

entries.note: Principle clarification pairs user-owned judgment with allowed mechanical aids like navigation and hygiene flags.
entries.reason: Deciding which causes matter was pushed onto the user, so the tool supplies everything.

entries.note: Blame avoidance is speculative past motivation; the principle is the user's requirement.
entries.reason: Keeping the model out of judgment avoids blame for wrong prioritization.

entries.note: Optional context intake passes the user's domain specifics into every agent prompt.
entries.reason: Users were assumed to hold better domain context than any sub-agent.

entries.note: plan --only lets users steer dispatch toward chosen branches.
entries.reason: No lightweight interaction lets users steer generation toward promising branches.

entries.note: Narrow single-job scoping is past design choice; nothing further actionable.
entries.reason: Separating generation from analysis narrowed the plugin's scope to one simple job.

entries.note: Navigation and partial reading make large output usable by subtree or top levels.
entries.reason: Output volume was not treated as a cost that degrades usability.

entries.note: Preview will report output reason and token counts, budgeting reading as well as generation.
entries.reason: Token budgets were considered for generation but not for reading the result.

entries.note: Loading guidance moves from whole-file reading to branch-by-branch paging with an index.

entries.reason: Human reading limits for thousands of reasons were never considered in the design.

entries.reason: Prototyping likely exercised small subtrees that did not reveal full-tree weight.

entries.note: Speed of v0.1.0 construction is past process; nothing further actionable.

entries.note: Beam or best-first expansion depends on declined scoring.

entries.note: Recruiting reviewers is a social remedy, not a plugin change.

entries.note: Showcase appeal of parallel fan-out is past motivation; no artifact change follows.

entries.note: Preview with confirmation bounds full-size runs by requiring user approval of reason and token counts.

entries.note: Implement-first AI-assisted building describes past process; no artifact change follows.
