entries.note: README known-limitations and design-decisions sections will record scale risks.
entries.reason: No design document listed scale risks for early sign-off.

entries.note: Parameterized shape replaces literals scattered across script, prompts and examples with stored run shape.
entries.reason: The fixed shape was embedded across multiple files before its costs were recognized.

entries.note: assemble writes an index.md of levels 1-2; summary and pruning layers stay declined under R-01.
entries.reason: Assembly flattens everything into one file with no summary, pruning, or index layer.

entries.note: The deferred post-processing that matters here is navigation: show, a levels 1-2 index.md and branch-by-branch loading guidance.
entries.reason: The v0.1.0 scope targeted a working end-to-end pipeline and deferred all post-processing layers.

entries.note: Explains how design effort went to orchestration in v0.1.0; the navigation gap it caused is covered by IMP-09.
entries.reason: The parallel fan-out orchestration was the novel, risky part and absorbed most design effort.

entries.note: Unknown sub-agent failure modes get explicit semantics: attempts recorded per task, stuck tasks reported, agents reply FAILED.
entries.reason: Coordinating 26 sub-agents in parallel had unknown failure modes that demanded attention first.

entries.note: Claude Code's dispatch limits and their documentation are platform facts; the plugin only documents the 20 cap it hit.
entries.reason: Claude Code sub-agent dispatch limits and behaviors were poorly documented at build time.

entries.note: Past iteration on fragment paths and merge ordering; the assembler is deterministic now, nothing further to change.
entries.reason: Fragment path conventions and merge ordering took several iterations to make deterministic.

entries.note: Past risk weighting that favored orchestration; readability work is now covered by IMP-09 and IMP-10.
entries.reason: Orchestration failure seemed fatal while unreadable output seemed merely inconvenient.

entries.note: Describes where prototype debugging time went; no remaining artifact change follows from it.
entries.reason: Early prototypes broke at dispatch, so debugging time concentrated there.

entries.note: Solo time constraint explains the v0.1.0 cut; the cut features themselves are covered by catalog improvements.
entries.reason: Limited solo developer time forced cutting features beyond generation.

entries.note: Side-project circumstance of the author; not something a plugin change addresses.
entries.reason: The plugin is a personal side project built in spare hours alongside a day job.

entries.note: Implied remedy of recruiting collaborators is organizational, not a plugin change.
entries.reason: No collaborators existed to split generation and presentation work in parallel.

entries.note: A stdlib unittest suite covering assemble, show, hygiene and waves lowers the upkeep cost of added layers.
entries.reason: Each additional layer would need its own prompts, validation, and fixtures to maintain.

entries.note: Ship-fast priority behind v0.1.0; nothing further actionable beyond existing improvements.
entries.reason: Shipping quickly to try the idea was valued over completeness.

entries.note: Author habit of minimal first versions; the later extensions are the catalog improvements.
entries.reason: Personal tooling habits favor minimal first versions extended later on demand.

entries.note: Consumption is now defined: show subtrees, a levels 1-2 index.md, and loading guidance that pages branch by branch.
entries.reason: No written requirements defined how the user would actually consume the output.

entries.note: Origin of the plugin as a mechanical 5x5 idea; the reading workflow is addressed by IMP-09.
entries.reason: The plugin started from a mechanical five-by-five idea rather than a user workflow.

entries.note: No persona was written for v0.1.0; user research itself is out of scope under R-06.
entries.reason: No target user persona was described beyond the author personally.

entries.note: Assembled header and run.json record bytes, approximate tokens and per-level counts, giving a measurable size baseline.
entries.reason: No acceptance criteria stated a token budget or reading time for results.

entries.note: Where early spec effort went; downstream use is now handled by IMP-09 navigation.
entries.reason: Spec effort went into the tree shape and validation schema instead of downstream use.

entries.note: README records design decisions (stdlib-only, generation-only) and limitations, capturing what chat sessions never preserved.
entries.reason: Design discussions happened in chat sessions that were never captured as a durable spec.

entries.note: Assumption that post-processing could be bolted on later; the actual additions are IMP-06, IMP-09 and IMP-10.
entries.reason: Post-processing was assumed easy to bolt on later without restructuring.

entries.note: Fragments do persist on disk; this merely explains the deferral, nothing further to change.
entries.reason: Fragment files persist on disk, suggesting any later pass could simply reread them.

entries.note: Principle clarification resolves the collision: mechanical aids allowed, summaries and interpretation stay with the user.
entries.reason: The author underestimated how summaries would collide with the no-analysis principle.

entries.note: Version-number psychology behind shipping v0.1.0 with gaps; no artifact change implied.
entries.reason: The 0.1.0 version number signaled permission to ship with known gaps.

entries.note: Deciding a summary format is moot: plugin-side summaries are declined because analysis belongs to the user.
entries.reason: Deferring was cheaper than deciding a summary format under uncertainty.

entries.note: Author's past project experience as motivation; nothing actionable in the plugin.
entries.reason: Past projects successfully added reporting after their core pipelines stabilized.

entries.note: A non-blocking hygiene report adds duplicate, restatement and length checks beyond shape validation.
entries.reason: Passing shape validation was treated as the definition of done.

entries.note: Pass/fail shape check stays; hygiene.json adds mechanical content flags so shape is no longer the only signal.
entries.reason: The check command gives a crisp pass or fail that is easy to declare complete.

entries.note: Stdlib heuristics (duplicates, near-duplicates, parent restatements, over-length) give objective proxies without judging causal quality.
entries.reason: Content-quality metrics for causal reasons have no obvious objective formula.

entries.note: An eval suite runs a smoke-preset run end to end and grades shape validity and hygiene report presence.
entries.reason: No evaluation harness existed to measure usefulness of the assembled output.

entries.note: Shape remains the blocking stop condition; an LLM judge in the fix loop is declined as flaky and costly.
entries.reason: Agent loops need a machine-verifiable stop condition, and shape was the one available.

entries.note: Reading experience is addressed by show, a levels 1-2 index.md, and branch-by-branch loading guidance.
entries.reason: Self-review focused on structural correctness rather than the reading experience.

entries.note: Summarizing and pruning remain declined; analysis belongs to the user, with hygiene flags and navigation as allowed aids.
entries.reason: The design principle that analysis belongs to the user forbids the plugin from summarizing or pruning.

entries.note: Summaries are interpretation the user's requirement reserves for them; the plugin keeps declining them.
entries.reason: Summaries were seen as analysis that could bias the user's own judgment.

entries.note: Condensing implies priority, which is plugin-side ranking and stays declined.
entries.reason: Condensing reasons implicitly signals which causes matter most.

entries.note: Avoiding model-chosen root causes is exactly why root-cause selection stays with the user.
entries.reason: The author worried users anchor on plausible-sounding but wrong model-chosen root causes.

entries.note: Five Whys methodology tradition is an external cultural fact, not a plugin property.
entries.reason: Five Whys tradition emphasizes a team discovering root causes themselves.

entries.note: Principle clarification explicitly separates neutral mechanical aids like navigation from interpretive summaries.
entries.reason: No distinction was drawn between neutral navigation aids and interpretive summaries.

entries.note: Author's prior bad experiences with AI summaries as motivation; the rule itself is clarified by IMP-15.
entries.reason: Earlier experiences with AI summaries hiding important details made the author wary.

entries.note: Pruning weak reasons is evaluation, which the catalog declines; hygiene flags annotate without deleting.
entries.reason: Pruning requires judging which reasons are weak, which is explicitly an evaluation.

entries.note: Trees stay complete; deleting reasons to break the five-per-node invariant is declined.
entries.reason: Deleting reasons would break the exact five-per-node invariant the validator enforces.

entries.note: Hygiene report defines concrete mechanical criteria for duplicates, restatements and over-length reasons, flagging without deleting.
entries.reason: No criteria for weak, duplicate, or off-topic reasons were ever defined.

entries.note: Model-made pruning is declined altogether, so auditing it is unnecessary.
entries.reason: Model-made pruning decisions are hard to audit after the fact.

entries.note: Assemble compares the whole tree for exact and near-duplicates across branches, flagging them rather than collapsing.
entries.reason: Collapsing duplicates across branches needs cross-fragment comparison nobody implemented.

entries.note: Completeness of every tree is a user requirement; dropping reasons is declined.
entries.reason: The completeness of all 3,905 reasons was itself treated as a selling point.

entries.note: The blanket rule gains an explicit carve-out for mechanical aids in skill, agent and README.
entries.reason: The principle is written as a blanket prompt rule with no exceptions.

entries.note: why-expander.md indeed says do not analyze, summarize, or rank; IMP-15 adds the mechanical-aid carve-out.
entries.reason: The why-expander instructions say do not analyze, summarize, or rank, with no carve-out.

entries.note: SKILL.md repeats the rule to the orchestrator; clarification updates both layers consistently.
entries.reason: The skill prompt repeats the same rule to the orchestrator, reinforcing it at every layer.

entries.note: Rationale for short absolute rules; the needed nuance is added by IMP-15.
entries.reason: Short absolute rules were preferred because models follow them more reliably than nuanced ones.

entries.note: Revisiting the rule is exactly the principle clarification pass across skill, agent and README.
entries.reason: Nobody revisited the rule after deciding the output would be read whole.

entries.note: Clarification adds text naming permitted structural aids: hygiene flags, navigation, measurement.
entries.reason: The prompts lack any section describing permitted structural aids like indexes.

entries.note: Keeping interpretation out of the plugin is the user's requirement; an in-plugin analysis mode is declined.
entries.reason: The plugin positions itself purely as a generator, pushing interpretation to a later conversation.

entries.note: Follow-up sessions are supported by show subtrees and loading guidance that pages branch by branch.
entries.reason: The expected workflow assumes the user asks Claude follow-up questions after loading the file.

entries.note: A separate analysis agent would do plugin-side synthesis, which stays declined.
entries.reason: Offloading analysis to the main session avoided designing a separate analysis agent.

entries.note: A show subcommand now exists for exploration; IMP-09 adds index.md and skill loading guidance using it.
entries.reason: The skill ends at assembly, with no follow-up command or exploration mode defined.

entries.note: Simplicity-of-description motivation for narrow scope; nothing to change.
entries.reason: Narrow responsibilities made the plugin simpler to explain in its one-line description.

entries.note: README states known limitations, including that no analysis step is bundled, instead of assuming other skills exist.
entries.reason: Composability with other analysis skills was assumed without verifying any exist.

entries.note: Clarification distinguishes indexes (mechanical navigation) from summaries (interpretation), so the rule no longer excludes both.
entries.reason: Index layers were conflated with summaries and excluded by the same rule.

entries.note: Adds the missing vocabulary separating structural metadata and navigation from interpretive content.
entries.reason: No design vocabulary separated structural metadata from interpretive content.

entries.note: index.md of levels 1-2 is verbatim structure, not a summary, and is explicitly planned.
entries.reason: An index of level-1 and level-2 reasons looks like a summary on paper.

entries.note: Labeling clusters by cause category is interpretive judgment and stays with the user.
entries.reason: Clustering by cause category would require labeling, which feels like judgment.

entries.note: Navigation aids are now enumerated concretely: show, index.md of levels 1-2, branch paging guidance.
entries.reason: The author never listed candidate navigation aids to evaluate them individually.

entries.note: Ids alone proved insufficient; show prints subtrees with ancestor chains and index.md lists levels 1-2.
entries.reason: Line-per-reason ids were considered sufficient indexing by themselves.

entries.note: Model access inside the script would need API keys and network, breaking the offline zero-dependency install.
entries.reason: The assembler is a deterministic Python script with no model access to condense or organize content.

entries.note: Mechanical-only assembly remains intentional; README documents the stdlib-only, generation-only design decision.
entries.reason: The script was deliberately limited to mechanical merge and validation to stay reliable.

entries.note: Reproducibility rationale for deterministic code still holds; nothing to change.
entries.reason: Deterministic code gives reproducible output that is easy to debug.

entries.note: In-script model calls requiring API keys and network access are declined.
entries.reason: Model calls inside the script would require API keys and network access.

entries.note: Awkwardness of invoking Claude recursively from Bash is a Claude Code platform property.
entries.reason: Plugin scripts run through Bash, where invoking Claude recursively is awkward.

entries.note: Author's division of trust between code and models; remains the design, nothing further actionable.
entries.reason: The author trusted code for invariants and models only for content generation.

entries.note: Retries and timeouts for in-script model calls are moot since such calls are declined.
entries.reason: Retries and timeouts for in-script model calls were work nobody wanted to write.

entries.note: A post-assembly model synthesis pass is plugin-side synthesis, which is declined.
entries.reason: Nothing in the pipeline schedules a model pass after assembly.

entries.note: Skill correctly ends at assembly; adding a synthesis step afterward is declined.
entries.reason: The skill's orchestration steps end once the check and assemble commands succeed.

entries.note: Synthesis agent is declined regardless of its cost.
entries.reason: A synthesis agent would cost another large context read of all fragments.

entries.note: A summary agent is declined; the size problem is handled by navigation (IMP-09) instead.
entries.reason: A single summary agent would itself hit the 150k-token size problem it aims to solve.

entries.note: Hierarchical per-branch summarization is still summarization and stays declined.
entries.reason: Hierarchical per-branch summarization was never considered during fan-out design.

entries.note: Per-branch digests flowing upward would be generated summaries; agents keep replying only OK or FAILED.
entries.reason: Sub-agents return only an OK line, so no per-branch digest flows back upward.

entries.note: Clustering or embedding libraries would break the zero-dependency offline install; stdlib heuristics substitute.
entries.reason: Standard-library-only Python rules out clustering or embedding libraries.

entries.note: Absence of guaranteed third-party packages on user machines is an ecosystem fact.
entries.reason: Plugins cannot count on third-party packages being installed on user machines.

entries.note: Claude Code providing no dependency management for plugin scripts is a platform fact.
entries.reason: Claude Code offers no standard dependency management for plugin scripts.

entries.note: Embedding models needing downloads or API calls are declined for the offline script.
entries.reason: Embedding models need downloads or API calls incompatible with offline assumptions.

entries.note: Author's pip conflicts as motivation for stdlib-only; the decision stands under R-02.
entries.reason: Recurring pip conflicts in the author's environment discourage adding dependencies.

entries.note: Hygiene report uses stdlib token-overlap similarity for near-duplicate detection.
entries.reason: Simple text similarity such as difflib was never tried for duplicate detection.

entries.note: Navigation is derived from ids and depth, which assembled trees carry, so no extra schema metadata is needed.
entries.reason: The fragment schema carries only reason text, leaving no metadata to build an index from.

entries.note: Category tags would be interpretive labeling; IMP-08 even removes the fixed cause-kind checklist.
entries.reason: Agents were never asked to tag reasons with a cause category.

entries.note: Validator-simplicity rationale for a minimal schema still holds; nothing to change.
entries.reason: Extra fields would widen the validator and increase fragment errors.

entries.note: Token-saving rationale for the minimal schema remains valid; no change implied.
entries.reason: A minimal schema kept token output lower across 25 branch agents.

entries.note: Tagging that nudges self-ranking conflicts with the declined plugin-side ranking.
entries.reason: Tagging was feared to nudge agents toward self-ranking, contradicting the principle.

entries.note: True: examples show only reason and whys, intentionally; adding tag keys is declined under R-01.
entries.reason: The shape example in prompts shows only reason and whys keys.

entries.note: assemble gains a second output, index.md of levels 1-2, alongside the JSON.
entries.reason: Output writing is a single dump function rather than pluggable renderers.

entries.note: Fastest-path rationale for one writer in v0.1.0; later outputs covered by IMP-09 and IMP-06.
entries.reason: One JSON writer was the fastest path to a testable artifact.

entries.note: A second output, index.md, is now planned for navigation.
entries.reason: No second output format was requested, so no abstraction emerged.

entries.note: The unittest suite covers assemble, hygiene and show, motivating clean separation of outputs.
entries.reason: No tests exist that would motivate separating rendering from assembly.

entries.note: A lightweight Markdown view (index.md of levels 1-2) is adopted; a full HTML viewer stays declined under R-05.
entries.reason: Markdown or HTML views were considered cosmetic next to pipeline correctness.

entries.note: Single-file JSON for whole-context reading is the user's requirement and stays.
entries.reason: The single-file writer matched the plan to paste the whole result into context.

entries.note: A full real run completed on 2026-09-13: 26 agents, 3,905 reasons, about 128k tokens output.
entries.reason: No full real run has happened, so the burden of a 150k-token file was never felt.

entries.note: A 3x3 smoke preset and plan --only make rehearsal cheap instead of spending a full 26-agent run.
entries.reason: A full run costs 26 sub-agent invocations, making the author reluctant to spend it on testing.

entries.note: init --model lets runs choose sonnet or haiku instead of inheriting the most expensive session model.
entries.reason: Default-model inheritance means every branch runs on the most expensive model.

entries.note: Stalled or failed tasks get recorded attempts and stuck reporting; re-running plan already resumes missing fragments.
entries.reason: Rate limits on parallel agents could stall or fail a test run midway.

entries.note: Unit tests exercise assemble with generated fixture fragments, no live model run needed.
entries.reason: No mock mode generates fake fragments to exercise assembly at full size.

entries.note: Cost and size preview with confirmation lets users judge usage-cap impact before a full run.
entries.reason: Subscription usage caps make large experimental runs feel wasteful.

entries.note: No longer relying on partial runs: a full 3,905-reason run completed on 2026-09-13.
entries.reason: Partial runs seemed enough to prove the merge logic worked.

entries.note: A full-size tree was produced and inspected: 3,905 reasons, 511 KB, on 2026-09-13.
entries.reason: Only small or partial trees were inspected during development.

entries.note: Development is no longer limited to reduced depth; a full 5x5x5x5x5 run completed on 2026-09-13.
entries.reason: Development used reduced depth where output fit comfortably on screen.

entries.note: Navigation problems at thousands of lines are addressed by show, index.md and branch paging guidance.
entries.reason: Tiny outputs hide navigation problems that appear at thousands of lines.

entries.note: init --breadth/--depth parameterizes the shape, allowing mid-size rehearsal runs.
entries.reason: The hard-coded 5x5 shape offered no mid-size setting for realistic rehearsal.

entries.note: Aggregate burden is made visible: bytes, approximate tokens and per-level word averages recorded in output.
entries.reason: Inspecting fragments one at a time masked the aggregate reading burden.

entries.note: Size is now measured from the real file (511 KB, about 128k tokens) and recorded in header and run.json.
entries.reason: Output size was estimated arithmetically rather than measured from a real file.

entries.note: Recruiting outside users to try the plugin is a social remedy, not a plugin change.
entries.reason: No user besides the author has tried the plugin and reported friction.

entries.note: The plugin is published publicly at github.com/JoshuaRamirez/five-whys and listed in the RedJay marketplace.
entries.reason: The plugin has not been published or shared for feedback yet.

entries.note: The public GitHub repository has issues enabled, providing a feedback channel.
entries.reason: No feedback channel or issue tracker is set up for the plugin.

entries.note: Recruiting colleagues for usability tests is organizational, not a plugin change.
entries.reason: Colleagues were not recruited for informal usability tests.

entries.note: Honest README with limitations, cost, real excerpt and design decisions eases newcomer confusion the author cannot see.
entries.reason: The author's familiarity with the design masks confusion a newcomer would feel.

entries.note: Releases are not local-only; the plugin is public on GitHub and listed in the RedJay marketplace.
entries.reason: Releases install from a local cache without any beta audience.

entries.note: Consumption has been exercised: the real 3,905-reason tree is being read via the new show subcommand in this self-improvement pass.
entries.reason: The consumption step was imagined rather than prototyped.

entries.note: Rather than one 128k-token read, loading guidance pages branch by branch with show and index.md.
entries.reason: Nobody tested whether Claude reasons usefully over 150k tokens of reasons in one read.

entries.note: Comprehension limits are mitigated by partial reading: show subtrees, index.md, branch paging guidance.
entries.reason: Context-window capacity was assumed to equal usable comprehension.

entries.note: Lookups now use show --id, printing a subtree with its ancestor chain instead of grepping ids.
entries.reason: The author expected the main session to handle lookups by grepping ids.

entries.note: The eval suite provides a scripted end-to-end scenario exercising a smoke run and its outputs.
entries.reason: No scenario scripts described a user answering a concrete question with the output.

entries.note: Research not consulted during design; the practical remedy, partial reading, is IMP-09.
entries.reason: Long-context degradation findings were not consulted during design.

entries.note: The self-improvement tree, catalog and ledger record this critique and tie each change to its reason.
entries.reason: The gap was identified only by a rating after implementation was finished.

entries.note: Timing of review in the v0.1.0 process; nothing further to change in the plugin.
entries.reason: Review happened at the end instead of at a design checkpoint before building.

entries.note: Absence of a personal design review template is process history, not a plugin artifact.
entries.reason: No design review template asks how outputs will be read and used.

entries.note: Build-before-design preference for a small plugin; no plugin change follows.
entries.reason: Building felt faster than writing a design document for a small plugin.

entries.note: The self-run is kept as dogfooding evidence in docs/self-improvement.
entries.reason: Running five-whys on itself is the first structured critique the plugin received.

entries.note: Incremental-release rationale for skipping design review; nothing actionable.
entries.reason: Planned incremental releases made up-front design review seem unnecessary.

entries.note: Human navigation is added on top of the grep-friendly format: show, index.md, branch paging guidance.
entries.reason: The output format was chosen for grep and validation convenience rather than human navigation.

entries.note: Line-per-reason format remains useful for tools; navigation needs are covered by IMP-09.
entries.reason: Line-per-reason formatting was picked so shell tools could extract individual items.

entries.note: Author's grep and sed workflow as motivation; nothing to change.
entries.reason: The author's workflow leans heavily on grep and sed for inspecting files.

entries.note: Valid rationale for one line per reason; the format stays.
entries.reason: Pretty-printed nested JSON would spread one reason over many lines.

entries.note: Diff-friendliness rationale still holds; no change implied.
entries.reason: Flat lines with ids make diffs across runs easy to compare.

entries.note: A curated navigation layer (show, index.md of levels 1-2) now complements grep.
entries.reason: Grep access was assumed to substitute for a curated index.

entries.note: Read tool truncation of long files is Claude Code platform behavior.
entries.reason: Agent Read tools truncate long files, so line addressing seemed a workaround.

entries.note: One file for whole-context reading is the user's requirement and stays.
entries.reason: A single file simplifies handing the result onward in one Read call.

entries.note: Rationale for a single file still holds under the user's one-JSON requirement.
entries.reason: Multiple files would require the user or agent to know which one to open.

entries.note: True today and intended; the skill reports one output path.
entries.reason: The skill's final message points at one path, keeping instructions short.

entries.note: Cleanup-simplicity rationale for single-file output; nothing to change.
entries.reason: Per-level file layouts would complicate cleanup of run directories.

entries.note: assemble --partial writes a valid tree with explicit missing-branch markers instead of producing nothing.
entries.reason: Atomic single-file writes avoid partially assembled outputs on failure.

entries.note: Whole-file reading is now complemented by loading guidance that pages branch by branch.
entries.reason: The idea of reading everything at once was never challenged by anyone.

entries.note: JSON output is the user's stated requirement and remains.
entries.reason: JSON was chosen for machine readability over human scanning.

entries.note: Reuse rationale for JSON still valid; no change.
entries.reason: The validator and assembler already speak JSON, so reuse avoided conversion code.

entries.note: Imagined programmatic use as motivation for JSON; nothing actionable.
entries.reason: Downstream programmatic analysis was imagined as a future use case.

entries.note: A Markdown view is limited to index.md of levels 1-2, avoiding a 3,905-bullet outline.
entries.reason: A Markdown outline with 3,905 bullets was judged equally unreadable.

entries.note: Unambiguous ids rationale for structured format still holds.
entries.reason: Structured formats keep ids and parent links unambiguous.

entries.note: A collapsible HTML viewer is declined heavy infrastructure; file-based show and index.md cover navigation.
entries.reason: Progressive-disclosure formats like collapsible HTML were never considered.

entries.note: Trees stay complete by requirement; relevance-based omission of branches is declined.
entries.reason: The fixed tree depth emits every branch in full regardless of relevance.

entries.note: Early-stop parameters are declined; IMP-01 configures uniform shape only, every tree complete.
entries.reason: The hard-coded 5x5 shape has no parameter to stop a branch early.

entries.note: Early stopping is declined, and judging root causes belongs to the user anyway.
entries.reason: Early stopping would require judging when a true root cause is reached.

entries.note: Uniform prompts rationale for fixed depth still holds; nothing to change.
entries.reason: Uniform depth kept agent prompts identical across all 25 branches.

entries.note: Variable-depth trees are declined, so validator complexity for them never arises.
entries.reason: Variable-depth trees would complicate the fragment validator's depth check.

entries.note: Exhaustive enumeration remains the plugin's defining intent per the user's requirement.
entries.reason: Exhaustive enumeration was the plugin's defining novelty.

entries.note: init and plan report reason counts and measured token estimates, confirming before full-size runs.
entries.reason: No token budget was set for the output, so size never constrained format choices.

entries.note: Output bytes and approximate tokens are measured and recorded in the header and run.json.
entries.reason: Per-reason overhead from ids and JSON punctuation was never measured.

entries.note: Size is now measured, not estimated: the real run produced about 128k tokens, recorded in output.
entries.reason: The format was designed before computing that 3,905 reasons approach 150k tokens.

entries.note: Million-token context windows are a model platform fact outside the plugin's control.
entries.reason: One-million-token context windows made 150k feel affordable.

entries.note: The test suite can assert assembled output properties including size for given shapes.
entries.reason: No test asserts a maximum assembled output size.

entries.note: Repeated reading cost is cut by partial reading: show subtrees and index.md instead of reloading everything.
entries.reason: Cost concerns focused on generation, not on repeatedly reading the result.

entries.note: show subcommand exists; loading guidance will page branch by branch rather than assuming whole-file reads.
entries.reason: Reading the whole file into context was assumed instead of querying or paging branches on demand.

entries.note: Consumption gets designed: show subtrees, index.md of levels 1-2, and branch-by-branch loading guidance.
entries.reason: Design attention went to generating the tree, leaving how anyone would consume it largely unexamined.

entries.note: Explains where v0.1.0 design effort went; consumption tooling itself is covered by IMP-09.
entries.reason: Orchestrating 26 parallel sub-agents was the novel challenge, so it absorbed most design effort.

entries.note: Builder motivation behind the fan-out focus; nothing further to change in the plugin.
entries.reason: Parallel fan-out offered visible technical difficulty that rewarded the builder's curiosity more than reading ergonomics.

entries.note: Past prioritization of blocking agent-limit problems; the concurrency cap fix is already committed.
entries.reason: Sub-agent limits and prompt generation raised immediate blocking problems that demanded attention first.

entries.note: A fact about ecosystem plugin examples, which this plugin cannot change.
entries.reason: Ecosystem plugin examples showcase agents doing work, rarely showing downstream retrieval of large outputs.

entries.note: Post-assembly consumption becomes active work: show, index.md and loading guidance extend success past assembly.
entries.reason: Early iterations counted a finished assembly as success, so later steps never became active work.

entries.note: Cost and size preview presents scale as a cost the user confirms, not a headline achievement.
entries.reason: The 3,905-reason target made scale itself feel like the headline achievement worth optimizing.

entries.note: Loading guidance and index.md define the post-assembly journey: scan levels 1-2, then page chosen branches.
entries.reason: No user journey was written for what happens after the assembled file exists.

entries.note: README gains design decisions, known limitations and measured costs, recording requirements beyond shape.
entries.reason: The project had no requirements document beyond the tree's shape specification.

entries.note: Honest documentation makes intent explicit for users other than the author.
entries.reason: The author expected to be the only user and relied on unstated personal intent.

entries.note: Principle clarification allows mechanical reading aids while keeping interpretation with the user.
entries.reason: Declaring analysis the user's job removed pressure to design any analysis interface.

entries.note: A plugin-side post-listing analysis workflow is declined; analysis stays with the user.
entries.reason: Classic Five Whys practice ends at listing causes, so post-listing workflow felt out of scope.

entries.note: Tracing one branch is now supported: show --id prints a subtree with its ancestor chain.
entries.reason: No concrete tasks, like tracing one branch to a root cause, were enumerated before building.

entries.note: Hygiene report adds quality signals beyond a structurally valid file, without ranking or summarizing.
entries.reason: Completion criteria centered on a valid file rather than on answering a user's question.

entries.note: Hygiene report flags duplicates, restatements and over-length reasons, so done means more than counts and nesting.

entries.reason: Structural rules are easy to automate, while usefulness needs human judgment no one scheduled.

entries.note: Claude Code does not expose subagent token usage to scripts; IMP-10 records output-size proxies.
entries.reason: Sub-agent token usage is not easily surfaced to plugin scripts.

entries.note: Account-level billing is an Anthropic platform fact outside plugin control.
entries.reason: Cost is billed at the account level, far from per-run design decisions.

entries.note: Init and plan will show agent count and measured token estimates, surfacing cost hidden by subscriptions.
entries.reason: Subscription plans hide the marginal token cost of a run from the user.

entries.note: File-based measurement in run.json replaces telemetry for usage accounting; no backend needed.
entries.reason: The pipeline has no telemetry hook for usage accounting.

entries.note: The cost half gets recorded per run; insight judgment stays with the user.
entries.reason: Cost-per-insight needs both a cost and an insight number, and neither existed.

entries.note: A full end-to-end run completed 2026-09-13: 26 agents, ~1.2M subagent tokens, ~7 minutes.
entries.reason: Token cost stayed invisible during design since the pipeline was never run end to end.

entries.note: Real run measured the output: 511 KB, about 128k tokens, not an estimate anymore.
entries.reason: The ~150k-token figure is an estimate rather than an observed measurement.

entries.note: README will document measured cost and time from the real run instead of an estimate.
entries.reason: Estimates are easy to discount compared with an actual bill or context overflow.

entries.note: Smoke preset (3 wide x 3 deep) and plan --only make rehearsal runs cheap and fast.
entries.reason: Running 26 agents end to end was slow and expensive to try during development.

entries.note: The 2026-09-13 full run produced the total output size, 511 KB, not just partial fragments.
entries.reason: Testing used partial fragments that never exposed the total output size.

entries.note: Plan and init will report token estimates grounded in the measured real-run output.
entries.reason: No tokenizer was run on a sample output to ground the number.

entries.note: Timing of the estimate relative to architecture is past process; measurement now exists.
entries.reason: The estimate emerged late, after the architecture was already set.

entries.note: Cost and size preview with confirmation brings output economics into every run.
entries.reason: Development focused on making orchestration mechanics work, not on output economics.

entries.note: Past allocation of development attention; economics are now handled by IMP-05 and IMP-10.
entries.reason: Parallel sub-agent dispatch was the novel, riskiest part and absorbed attention.

entries.note: Past prioritization of urgent assembly bugs; nothing further to change.
entries.reason: Fragment assembly bugs were concrete and urgent while cost stayed abstract.

entries.note: Engineering instinct during authoring; no artifact change beyond other codes.
entries.reason: Engineering instincts reward solving hard plumbing over questioning requirements.

entries.note: The preview reports reason count and token estimate, answering consumption cost before dispatch.
entries.reason: No design review step asked what the output would cost to consume.

entries.note: v0.1.0 success definition is past; quality signals are added via IMP-06 and IMP-18.
entries.reason: Success for v0.1.0 was defined as the pipeline running and assembling.

entries.note: Preview sums aggregate agents, reasons and tokens so distributed cost is visible upfront.
entries.reason: Generation cost is spread across isolated sub-agents, so no single context feels heavy.

entries.note: Whole-run agent, reason and token totals shown before dispatch counter per-agent cheapness.
entries.reason: Each branch agent sees only 155 reasons, which looks cheap in isolation.

entries.note: Assemble already prints bytes and approx_tokens, and the skill forbids reading the tree unless asked.
entries.reason: The orchestrator never sums fragment sizes before committing to read them.

entries.note: Recorded bytes, tokens, duration and attempts per run expose the aggregate fan-out cost.
entries.reason: Fan-out hides aggregate cost the way microservices hide total latency.

entries.note: A system budget is set by choosing breadth/depth at init, which all prompts derive from.
entries.reason: Per-agent prompts were tuned individually rather than against a system budget.

entries.note: Breadth and depth flags cap total reasons while keeping trees complete; truncation stays declined.
entries.reason: No budget parameter caps total reasons or tokens across agents.

entries.note: Show, index.md and branch-by-branch loading guidance replace assuming the whole file is readable.
entries.reason: Large context windows made a 150k-token file seem readable in principle.

entries.note: How 1M-token models shape user expectations is a model ecosystem fact.
entries.reason: 1M-token models encourage treating context as effectively unlimited.

entries.note: README known limitations will warn about long-context recall degradation when reading whole trees.
entries.reason: Recall and reasoning degradation over long contexts is invisible in a quick demo.

entries.note: Show subcommand exists; index.md and partial-reading guidance add the missing indexing.
entries.reason: Reading the file whole was assumed simpler than designing retrieval or indexing.

entries.note: index.md of levels 1-2 delivers the deferred index; summaries stay declined under R-01.
entries.reason: Summaries and indexes were deferred as a later-version concern.

entries.note: Loading guidance will page branch by branch instead of treating the context limit as the only bound.
entries.reason: Context limits were treated as a hard ceiling rather than a usability curve.

entries.note: init --model lets runs use cheaper models, with documented trade-offs.
entries.reason: Default-model execution was accepted without testing cheaper models for deep levels.

entries.note: Model choice recorded in run.json and passed as the Agent model override per task.
entries.reason: Per-agent model selection was never exposed as a choice in the agent frontmatter.

entries.note: Inherit remains default but becomes an explicit choice among inherit, sonnet, opus, haiku.
entries.reason: Inheriting the parent model avoids a decision and seems safest for quality.

entries.note: Docs will explain model quality-cost trade-offs; smoke runs allow cheap comparison.
entries.reason: No benchmark showed whether smaller models meaningfully degrade leaf reasons.

entries.note: Claude Code interface not surfacing per-model cost is a platform fact.
entries.reason: Cost differences between models are not surfaced in the Claude Code interface.

entries.note: Past sequencing judgment; model selection is now covered by IMP-04.
entries.reason: Optimizing cost before quality was proven felt premature.

entries.note: Principle clarification separates allowed mechanical aids from interpretation, so value questions are not wholly excluded.
entries.reason: Leaving analysis to the user pushed the question of value outside the plugin's scope.

entries.note: Avoiding ranking is the user's requirement; plugin-side ranking remains declined.
entries.reason: The plugin deliberately avoids ranking so the model cannot bias the user's judgment.

entries.note: Authoritative-but-wrong model picks justify keeping root-cause selection with the user.
entries.reason: Model-picked root causes can sound authoritative while being wrong.

entries.note: Docs will state helpful mechanical aids like hygiene flags and navigation fit within neutrality.
entries.reason: Neutrality was valued as a design principle above helpfulness.

entries.note: Ranking without user system context is exactly why ranking stays declined.
entries.reason: Ranking needs context about the user's system that the model lacks.

entries.note: Implied remedy is adding LLM synthesis; analysis remains the user's by requirement.
entries.reason: The author distrusts LLM synthesis more than LLM enumeration.

entries.note: Analogy to facilitated sessions explains past design; nothing further actionable.
entries.reason: Leaving judgment to humans mirrors traditional facilitated root-cause sessions.

entries.note: A synthesis stage is plugin-side analysis, which the user's requirement declines.
entries.reason: Without a synthesis stage, the pipeline has nowhere insight could be produced or measured.

entries.note: Assemble will also write hygiene.json, adding a mechanical artifact beyond the raw tree.
entries.reason: The pipeline ends at assembly, so its last observable artifact is the raw tree.

entries.note: Duplicate detection arrives as non-blocking flags; clustering and deletion stay declined.
entries.reason: Clustering or deduplication was seen as scope creep for v0.1.0.

entries.note: Synthesis over 3,905 reasons is declined; the cost argument reinforces that.
entries.reason: Synthesizing 3,905 reasons would itself need another costly large-context pass.

entries.note: Testing division-of-labor fit with real users is user research, not a plugin change.
entries.reason: The machine-generates, human-analyzes division of labor was never tested for fit.

entries.note: Defining and producing insight inside the plugin is analysis, which stays with the user.
entries.reason: A synthesis step would force a definition of insight, which was avoided.

entries.note: Navigation and partial reading reduce the need to read thousands of reasons at once.
entries.reason: The user was assumed to have time and attention to read thousands of reasons.

entries.note: Developer-as-user tolerance explains past design; reader burden is handled by IMP-09.
entries.reason: The developer-as-user has unusually high tolerance for raw output.

entries.note: Preview will show reason count before dispatch, making human reading volume explicit.
entries.reason: Human reading cost is not counted in token-centric design thinking.

entries.note: Clarification will state that Claude loading and navigating the tree on request is allowed, not forbidden analysis.
entries.reason: Expecting Claude to read it for the user conflicts with the no-analysis rule.

entries.note: README will include a real excerpt and usage guidance describing a realistic reader.
entries.reason: No persona or usage scenario described a realistic reader.

entries.note: Show prints an indented outline and index.md adds a skimmable levels 1-2 view for humans.
entries.reason: Line-per-reason formatting was optimized for machines rather than skimming humans.

entries.note: Hygiene report adds a mechanical quality signal so delivery alone is not the only criterion.
entries.reason: Handing off analysis made delivering the tree the plugin's success criterion by definition.

entries.note: Specificity instructions and examples raise the bar so generic complete filler is less acceptable.
entries.reason: Scoping value out of the tool lets any complete output count as done.

entries.note: Boundary simplicity was a sound past design rationale with nothing to change.
entries.reason: Clear boundaries simplify implementation and reduce ambiguous responsibilities.

entries.note: Honest README known limitations take ownership of what the design does not deliver.
entries.reason: Blame for a poor result shifts to the reader rather than the design.

entries.note: Generator positioning matches the user's requirement; becoming an advisor is declined.
entries.reason: The plugin description positions it as a generator, not an advisor.

entries.note: Checking whether users reached conclusions requires user research, outside the plugin.
entries.reason: No acceptance test checks whether a user actually reached a conclusion.

entries.note: Relative model reliability at generation versus judgment is a model capability fact.
entries.reason: Generating raw material is something LLMs do reliably, while trustworthy judgment is harder.

entries.note: Hygiene flags expose duplicates, restatements and over-length reasons that enumeration hides.
entries.reason: Enumeration prompts rarely fail visibly, giving the pipeline a high apparent success rate.

entries.note: Undetectable judgment errors reinforce keeping judgment with the user.
entries.reason: Judgment errors are harder to detect and could damage trust in the plugin.

entries.note: Maturity of generation versus evaluation tooling is an ecosystem fact.
entries.reason: Tooling for structured generation is more mature than tooling for evaluation.

entries.note: Common design heuristic explaining past choices; nothing further actionable.
entries.reason: Playing to model strengths is a common plugin design heuristic.

entries.note: Implied remedy is a ranked shortlist; ranking is declined, IMP-06 flags weak reasons instead.
entries.reason: Volume masks weak individual reasons, whereas a ranked shortlist would expose them.

entries.note: Cost preview with confirmation counters volume feeling free because wall-clock time stays low.
entries.reason: Parallel sub-agent fan-out made generating more reasons cheap in wall-clock time, rewarding volume.

entries.note: Low latency hides token cost; preview shows it. Note dispatch is now capped at 20 per round.
entries.reason: Running 25 branch agents concurrently keeps latency low regardless of total output.

entries.note: Which cost users notice most is a user-behavior fact outside plugin control.
entries.reason: Latency is the cost users notice most, so it dominated optimization.

entries.note: Showcasing Claude Code parallelism was past motivation; nothing further to change.
entries.reason: Parallelism is a showcase feature of Claude Code's sub-agent system.

entries.note: Small per-agent contexts are a sound past design rationale needing no change.
entries.reason: Concurrent dispatch keeps each agent's context small and avoids truncation.

entries.note: Preview and confirmation make parallel token spend visible even though the session is not slowed.
entries.reason: Tokens spent in parallel do not visibly slow the user's session.

entries.note: Past assumption about free throughput; visibility is covered by IMP-05 and IMP-10.
entries.reason: Throughput was treated as free once parallelism was available.

entries.note: Branch prompts will list other level-1/level-2 reasons as covered elsewhere.
entries.reason: Isolated branches cannot see each other, so nothing stops redundant generation.

entries.note: Sharing deeper sibling output serializes the run; declined in favor of the level-1/2 digest.
entries.reason: Sharing sibling output would reintroduce sequential dependency and latency.

entries.note: The cheap level-1/2 digest in each prompt provides coordination without a shared step.
entries.reason: Fragment files are written independently with no coordination step.

entries.note: Deliberate anti-anchoring isolation is past rationale; IMP-07 shares only the level-1/2 digest.
entries.reason: Isolation was chosen deliberately to prevent cross-branch anchoring.

entries.note: Assemble gains the overlap post-pass via hygiene.json near-duplicate detection.
entries.reason: Detecting overlap would require a post-pass the script does not have.

entries.note: Showing agents sibling level-1/2 reasons reinforces the partition instead of assuming it.
entries.reason: The root agent's level-2 split was assumed to partition causes cleanly.

entries.note: Implied remedy is unbalanced trees; the user requires complete trees, shape configurable via IMP-01.
entries.reason: The architecture rewarded symmetry, making a full balanced tree feel like a finished design.

entries.note: Neat id and fragment mapping explains past design; nothing further to change.
entries.reason: A balanced tree maps neatly onto ids, fragment files, and agent counts.

entries.note: Uneven trees and dynamic scheduling would drop completeness, which is declined.
entries.reason: Uneven trees would need dynamic scheduling the orchestrator lacks.

entries.note: Builder aesthetic preference is past psychology with no artifact change.
entries.reason: Builders often take aesthetic satisfaction in regular structures.

entries.note: Ease of explanation is past motivation; nothing further actionable.
entries.reason: Symmetry made the plugin simple to explain in its description.

entries.note: Pruning judgment calls are exactly what the plugin declines; analysis stays user-side.
entries.reason: Pruning logic introduces judgment calls the design sought to avoid.

entries.note: Adaptive stopping would drop complete trees, which the user's requirement forbids.
entries.reason: No adaptive stopping rule lets a branch end once its causes converge or repeat.

entries.note: Non-blocking hygiene flags detect children restating ancestors using stdlib overlap, without stopping branches.
entries.reason: Detecting convergence needs semantic comparison that shape checks cannot perform.

entries.note: Prompting agents to stop at a root cause means variable depth, which is declined.
entries.reason: Fixed depth is easier to prompt than asking agents to stop at a root cause.

entries.note: Specificity grounding, stated assumptions and specific-vs-generic examples reduce plausible filler at deep levels.
entries.reason: Models tend to produce plausible filler rather than declare a branch exhausted.

entries.note: Variable-depth fragments are declined; trees stay complete at the configured depth.
entries.reason: Variable-depth fragments would break the validator's fixed depth argument.

entries.note: Depth becomes a configurable init --depth instead of a fixed law of five.
entries.reason: Classic Five Whys uses depth five as a rule of thumb, which was treated as law.

entries.note: Init and plan will report agents, reasons and token estimates and confirm before full runs.
entries.reason: Sub-agent tokens are consumed without per-dispatch cost previews or warnings.

entries.note: Claude Code lacking pre-launch cost estimates is a platform fact; IMP-05 compensates in-plugin.
entries.reason: Claude Code shows no cost estimate before launching many agents.

entries.note: No sub-agent token budget control for plugin authors is a Claude Code platform limit.
entries.reason: Plugin authors cannot set token budgets on sub-agents directly.

entries.note: Delayed plan usage limits are an Anthropic billing fact outside plugin control.
entries.reason: Plan usage limits bite later, disconnected from the run that triggered them.

entries.note: The skill will show fan-out size and confirm with the user before a full-size dispatch.
entries.reason: Users approve the skill once and never see the size of the fan-out.

entries.note: Confirmation before full-size dispatch adds proportional friction to large runs.
entries.reason: Absent friction makes large dispatches feel as cheap as small ones.

entries.note: Shape is the core hard-coded element; parameterized breadth/depth stored in run.json starts turning the prototype into configurable engineering.
entries.reason: The plugin was built as a fixed prototype, leaving its shape, model choice, and evaluation unengineered.

entries.note: Directly addressed: plan, check, assemble and prompts read shape from run.json instead of BRANCHING/DEPTH module constants.
entries.reason: Fixing depth and breadth at five let the script hard-code validation and fragment-splitting constants.

entries.note: SKILL.md still hard-codes 3,905 and 26 agents; IMP-01 makes prompts, docs and examples read the stored shape.
entries.reason: With a fixed 5x5 shape, every count (5, 30, 155, 3,905) could be precomputed once and written as literals.

entries.note: Five feels definitional; init --breadth/--depth keeps 5/5 defaults while making the shape a tunable choice.
entries.reason: The Five Whys method is traditionally taught as exactly five levels, so the number felt definitional rather than tunable.

entries.note: Toyota-derived teaching convention of five levels is an industry fact outside the plugin.
entries.reason: Toyota-derived teaching materials present five as the canonical count, not as a heuristic default.

entries.note: Name encodes the method; defaults remain 5/5 per the user's requirement, so the name needs no change.
entries.reason: The plugin's name itself encodes five, making any other depth seem off-brand.

entries.note: Unsurveyed variants like three-whys become available as the 3x3 smoke preset; adaptive depth stays declined.
entries.reason: The author did not survey variants such as three-whys or adaptive-depth root cause analysis.

entries.note: The user did require the textbook 5x5x5x5x5; that motivation is accurate and defaults preserve it.
entries.reason: Expected users were assumed to want the textbook method verbatim rather than a tunable variant.

entries.note: README design decisions will record why breadth five is the default and that it is configurable.
entries.reason: No design note questioned whether breadth of five, unlike depth of five, has any methodological basis.

entries.note: The script already has a total_reasons(depth) helper computing sums of powers of BRANCHING.
entries.reason: Closed-form sums of powers of five are easy to do mentally, so no tree-size helper function seemed needed.

entries.note: plan, check and assemble share BRANCHING, DEPTH and total_reasons(); arithmetic is not repeated as literals.
entries.reason: Geometric series feel trivial, hiding how often the same arithmetic recurs across plan, check, and assemble.

entries.note: Script prompts compute totals, but SKILL.md reuses drafted literals (3,905, 20 then 5); IMP-01 derives them.
entries.reason: Totals were computed while drafting prompt text and those numbers were reused directly in code.

entries.note: fivewhys.py defines a shared constants block (BRANCHING, DEPTH, ROOT_DEPTH, BRANCH_DEPTH) at module top.
entries.reason: Single-file Python scripts of a few hundred lines rarely get a shared geometry or constants module.

entries.note: Neither 155 nor 3,905 appears in the script; both are computed from module constants.
entries.reason: No reviewer asked where 155 and 3,905 came from when reading the script.

entries.note: A size function exists: total_reasons(depth) with BRANCHING as a module constant.
entries.reason: Writing a size function forces choosing its signature, which invites the parameterization question being avoided.

entries.note: Exact counts stay required, but validation will read breadth and depth from run.json instead of constants.
entries.reason: Validation was designed to confirm structure matched expectations, and the expectations were exact numbers.

entries.note: Beyond list-length checks, assemble will write hygiene.json flagging duplicates, restatements and over-length reasons.
entries.reason: Shape validation was the only check implemented, so its logic centered entirely on matching list lengths.

entries.note: A range or configurable minimum would allow incomplete trees; exact complete fan-out is the user's requirement.
entries.reason: An exactly-five rule is simpler to express and explain than a range or configurable minimum.

entries.note: Concrete counts in errors help agents repair fragments; that remains desirable with a stored shape.
entries.reason: Error messages cite literal counts so agents can fix their fragments without interpreting formulas.

entries.note: plan and check already derive expectations from the same module constants, not independent literals.
entries.reason: Plan and check were written together, so their agreement was trusted rather than derived from shared parameters.

entries.note: JSON Schema validation would need the third-party jsonschema package, breaking the zero-dependency install.
entries.reason: No schema language such as JSON Schema was used, which would have naturally externalized the counts.

entries.note: The level-2 root/branch split becomes derived from the stored shape rather than tuned to 25 agents.
entries.reason: Splitting fragments at level two was tuned to one cost profile of twenty-five branch agents.

entries.note: Real ceiling is Claude Code's 20-subagent cap; plan will group tasks into waves no larger than the cap.
entries.reason: Twenty-five parallel sub-agents was judged the practical ceiling for concurrent dispatch in one session.

entries.note: Split point is derived per shape under IMP-01, with waves (IMP-03) handling larger agent counts.
entries.reason: Splitting at another level yields 5 or 125 agents, both of which seemed unworkable.

entries.note: Assembled header and run.json will record bytes, tokens, duration and attempts, giving measurements for split decisions.
entries.reason: The split point was chosen by reasoning about sizes, not by measuring agent runtime or token use.

entries.note: Rationale for picking 155-reason fragments; the derived split under IMP-01 covers any further action.
entries.reason: Only one split point produced roughly equal 155-reason fragments suited to a single agent's attention.

entries.note: A derived root/branch split computed from stored breadth and depth is the planner this reason says was missing.
entries.reason: Choosing splits dynamically needs a planner weighing agent limits against context size, which did not exist.

entries.note: Prompts already render computed numbers concretely via f-strings; the concreteness motivation needs no change.
entries.reason: Literal numbers make generated prompts concrete, which was prioritized to keep sub-agents from miscounting.

entries.note: Models following concrete numeric targets more reliably is a model behavior fact.
entries.reason: Models follow concrete targets like 155 reasons more reliably than symbolic formulas.

entries.note: Authoring history of prompt text; prompts are now formatted from constants, and IMP-01 finishes the job.
entries.reason: Prompt text was authored as filled-in examples first and only later wrapped in string formatting.

entries.note: Past reinforcement from early drafts; nothing further actionable beyond IMP-01.
entries.reason: Early prompt drafts that used literal numbers appeared to work, reinforcing the pattern.

entries.note: Readable plan output is a benefit worth keeping; no artifact change implied.
entries.reason: Readable plan output doubles as documentation for users inspecting what agents will be told.

entries.note: A templating library would add a third-party dependency; stdlib f-strings already suffice.
entries.reason: No templating library was used, so every computed value meant hand-built string formatting.

entries.note: A general tree specification is the shape stored in run.json that every subcommand reads.
entries.reason: The script was written against a single concrete run layout instead of a general tree specification.

entries.note: A second use case now exists: init --preset smoke gives a cheap 3x3 rehearsal.
entries.reason: Development targeted one motivating use case: a single tree of 3,905 reasons.

entries.note: The user did specify 5x5x5x5x5; accurate history, and defaults keep that shape.
entries.reason: The originating request specified five-by-five explicitly and no other shapes were ever requested.

entries.note: Build-order history; end-to-end first was reasonable and generalization now follows in IMP-01.
entries.reason: Work proceeded by making one pipeline succeed end to end before considering any generalization.

entries.note: The imagined three-by-three triage becomes the --preset smoke 3x3 shape.
entries.reason: No second use case, such as a quick three-by-three triage, was imagined during design.

entries.note: Framing history; exhaustiveness remains the user's requirement while the shape becomes adjustable.
entries.reason: The plugin was framed as a demonstration of exhaustive scale rather than an adjustable tool.

entries.note: README design decisions will write down requirements and parameters that previously lived only in conversation.
entries.reason: Requirements lived in conversation rather than a written spec that would list variable parameters.

entries.note: The two-root-level assumption goes away when the root/branch split is derived from the stored shape.
entries.reason: Ids and file names like branch-5.1 assume exactly two root levels and single-digit child indexes.

entries.note: Ids are parsed with split('.') and int(), so multi-digit child indexes already work.
entries.reason: Dotted single-digit ids were chosen because breadth never exceeded nine in the planned design.

entries.note: Human-scannable fragment names are a good choice and remain; nothing to change.
entries.reason: Fragment names were designed to be human-scannable for the known set of twenty-five branches.

entries.note: Segment counts tied to ROOT_DEPTH become derived from the stored depth and split.
entries.reason: Id handling likely splits on dots and assumes a fixed number of segments at each stage.

entries.note: unittest coverage of init, plan and assemble across shapes exercises alternate run structures.
entries.reason: The run directory layout was created once and never exercised with alternate structures.

entries.note: Enumerating expected ids is correct; assemble --partial will mark missing branches instead of failing outright.
entries.reason: Assembly locates fragments by enumerating expected ids rather than discovering which files exist.

entries.note: Subcommands will read shape from run.json rather than module globals.
entries.reason: Plan, check, and assemble live in one cohesive script sharing globals instead of functions taking a tree spec.

entries.note: Single-file stdlib script is a deliberate, kept decision (see R-02); no change implied.
entries.reason: A single-file script was preferred so the plugin ships without any package installation step.

entries.note: Globals remain defaults only; per-run shape comes from run.json under IMP-01.
entries.reason: Module-level globals are the most convenient home for values every subcommand needs.

entries.note: Passing the stored shape from run.json into plan, check and assemble fills the missing geometry object.
entries.reason: No data class representing tree geometry was introduced to pass between subcommands.

entries.note: Ecosystem norm of ad hoc plugin helper scripts is outside the plugin's control.
entries.reason: Claude Code plugins commonly bundle ad hoc helper scripts, setting a low structural bar.

entries.note: Deferral history; the parameterization refactor itself is IMP-01.
entries.reason: Refactoring into parameterized functions was deferred because the script felt small enough to hold in mind.

entries.note: SKILL.md's literal root-then-20-then-5 rounds become plan-emitted waves the skill dispatches in order.
entries.reason: The skill orchestrator is written to dispatch exactly one root agent followed by twenty-five branch agents.

entries.note: SKILL.md already loops: run plan, dispatch listed tasks, repeat until state is ready.
entries.reason: Skill markdown describes dispatch procedurally rather than iterating over whatever tasks the plan returns.

entries.note: Skills lacking a native loop construct is a Claude Code platform fact.
entries.reason: Skills have no native loop construct, so fixed step-by-step instructions were the natural format.

entries.note: Sequencing is generic: plan's state field returns root first, then branches, then ready.
entries.reason: Branches must wait on the root fragment, a sequencing constraint easiest to spell out literally.

entries.note: Explicit batch sizes become plan-emitted waves capped at the concurrency limit.
entries.reason: Parallel counts were stated explicitly to stop the model from batching or serializing agents differently.

entries.note: Skill prose will state counts from init/plan output instead of literals, so agent count can vary.
entries.reason: Changing agent count would require rewriting skill prose, so the script had no incentive to vary it.

entries.note: show subcommand, index.md of levels 1-2 and branch-by-branch loading guidance decouple reading from one token budget.
entries.reason: The one-line-per-reason output format was sized around a single known token budget of about 150k.

entries.note: The size one context can read whole is a model/platform limit.
entries.reason: Around 150k tokens was treated as the most one context could reasonably read whole.

entries.note: init and plan will report reason count and token estimates, and confirm before large runs.
entries.reason: Larger shapes like six-by-six would overflow context, so the format silently assumed today's total.

entries.note: Smaller shapes become first-class through the smoke preset.
entries.reason: Smaller shapes were not considered because the design goal was exhaustiveness, not brevity.

entries.note: Paged reading via show and index.md addresses output too large to read whole.
entries.reason: Assembly writes one file because chunked or paged output was never needed at the target size.

entries.note: Measured token estimates will be computed and reported for whatever shape a run uses.
entries.reason: Token estimates were only ever calculated for the exact 3,905-reason case.

entries.note: init --breadth/--depth is the missing CLI option carrying shape into the script.
entries.reason: No configuration file or CLI option existed to carry depth and breadth values into the script.

entries.note: The skill will pass optional breadth/depth through to init's flags; problem-only invocation keeps 5/5 defaults.
entries.reason: The skill is invoked with only a problem statement and defines no syntax for shape options.

entries.note: Slash-command arguments arriving as free text is a Claude Code platform fact.
entries.reason: Slash-command arguments arrive as free text, making structured numeric options awkward to parse.

entries.note: Prose-burden concern; IMP-01 lets argparse validate while the skill merely forwards values.
entries.reason: Supporting options would require the skill to explain and validate them in prose.

entries.note: One-line invocation stays available because breadth and depth default to 5.
entries.reason: A one-line invocation was wanted so users need not learn any parameters.

entries.note: Precedent in other plugins is past context with nothing further actionable.
entries.reason: No precedent in the author's other plugins used per-invocation numeric options.

entries.note: init --breadth/--depth are argparse flags, so the script, not the model, validates option values.
entries.reason: Model-side argument parsing is less reliable than argparse, discouraging options passed through the skill.

entries.note: run.json already records branching and depth, but subcommands ignore it; IMP-01 makes them read it.
entries.reason: The run directory has no manifest recording the chosen shape for later subcommands to read.

entries.note: plan and assemble already read run.json for the problem; only check takes just a path.
entries.reason: Plan, check, and assemble were designed as stateless calls that take only paths.

entries.note: run.json already exists with a schema field for versioning.
entries.reason: A persisted manifest would invite versioning and migration concerns not yet considered.

entries.note: run.json stores schema, problem, created, branching and depth, not only the problem.
entries.reason: The problem statement was the only metadata written when a run was created.
