entries.note: Recency and adoption of plugin eval features are ecosystem facts.
entries.reason: Eval features for plugins shipped recently and have not been widely adopted.

entries.note: Past lack of motivation to search; the 6/10 analysis now prompted IMP-18.
entries.reason: The author never searched for eval tooling because no failure prompted the need.

entries.note: Past time competition between learning evals and finishing; no further artifact change.
entries.reason: Learning a new eval framework competed directly with finishing the plugin itself.

entries.note: Discoverability of eval documentation is controlled by Anthropic.
entries.reason: Eval documentation is less discoverable than core plugin authoring documentation.

entries.note: Eval runs a whole smoke-preset fan-out end to end rather than a single prompt.
entries.reason: Existing eval harnesses target single prompts rather than multi-agent fan-out orchestration.

entries.note: Community testing norms for agent workflows are an industry culture fact.
entries.reason: The wider prompt-engineering community lacks norms for testing agent workflows.

entries.note: Craft-style prompt iteration is industry culture outside the plugin.
entries.reason: Prompt work is often treated as craft iterated by feel rather than engineered against specs.

entries.note: Pace of agentic workflow versus verification methods is an industry fact.
entries.reason: Agentic multi-step workflows emerged faster than methods for verifying them.

entries.note: Shared plugins rarely including tests is ecosystem culture.
entries.reason: Popular shared plugins and prompts rarely include tests, normalizing their absence.

entries.note: Showcase culture favoring outputs over evaluations is industry culture.
entries.reason: Success stories showcase impressive outputs rather than reproducible evaluation results.

entries.note: Evaluation research focus on models is outside plugin control.
entries.reason: Evaluation research focuses on models themselves, not on user-built orchestrations.

entries.note: Building a benchmark dataset of known-good Five Whys trees is out of scope as a non-plugin activity.
entries.reason: No benchmark of known-good Five Whys trees exists to score output quality against.

entries.note: No single correct tree exists, so the eval grades objective shape validity and hygiene report presence instead of a gold reference.
entries.reason: Five Whys trees have no single correct answer, so a known-good tree is hard to define.

entries.note: Omitted context is addressed by optional context intake stored in run.json and included in every prompt.
entries.reason: Causal analysis depends on context the problem statement omits, so many different trees are defensible.

entries.note: Short prompts without system data get an optional context field the skill passes to every agent.
entries.reason: Problem statements given to the plugin are short prompts with no attached system data.

entries.note: The skill will ask once for key specifics when the problem statement is thin.
entries.reason: The plugin never asks clarifying questions before expanding the tree.

entries.note: Agent instruction 'assume typical context' is replaced by grounding in problem specifics and explicit stated assumptions.
entries.reason: Agents are told to assume typical context rather than request specifics.

entries.note: Context intake lets users paste log excerpts or interview notes that a bare problem statement lacks.
entries.reason: Real incidents rely on logs and interviews that a text prompt cannot carry.

entries.note: Past scoping decision for the prototype; the actionable part is covered by IMP-16 context intake.
entries.reason: Context capture was considered out of scope for a lightweight prototype.

entries.note: A consensus expert reference tree requires recruiting experts, a social remedy outside the plugin.
entries.reason: Experts disagree on root causes, so no consensus reference tree can be produced.

entries.note: Practitioners' choice of RCA frameworks is an industry fact no plugin change affects.
entries.reason: Practitioners use different frameworks such as fishbone diagrams, fault trees, and Five Whys.

entries.note: Reviewer domain bias is a human trait outside the plugin's control.
entries.reason: Reviewers bring domain biases that steer them toward causes in their own specialty.

entries.note: An adjudication process for competing expert trees is organizational work, not a plugin change.
entries.reason: No adjudication process exists to reconcile competing expert trees.

entries.note: Rarely measured inter-rater agreement is a field-wide research practice fact.
entries.reason: Inter-rater agreement on causal judgments is rarely measured, so its low level goes unnoticed.

entries.note: Five Whys lacks a formal definition industry-wide; the agent file already defines a cause operationally as answering why the parent happens.
entries.reason: Five Whys has no formal definition of what counts as a valid cause.

entries.note: Implied remedy is fewer or variable reasons per node; the user requires complete trees, though shape becomes configurable.
entries.reason: The 5x5 fan-out forces reasons real analyses would never produce, so no natural reference matches it.

entries.note: Single-chain human practice implies narrowing fan-out; complete 5-wide trees are the user's requirement.
entries.reason: Human Five Whys usually follows one chain, not five parallel reasons per level.

entries.note: Implied 'not applicable' slots or variable fan-out are declined; every tree stays complete.
entries.reason: Genuine problems rarely have exactly five distinct causes at every node.

entries.note: The 5x5x5x5x5 shape came from the user's stated requirement, not a symmetry preference.
entries.reason: The fixed shape was chosen for symmetry and parallelism rather than causal fidelity.

entries.note: Padding shows up as near-duplicates or parent restatements, which the hygiene report flags without deleting.
entries.reason: Padding reasons to reach five dilutes any reference a human would author.

entries.note: No human-authored 3,905-node reference exists anywhere; nothing the plugin can change creates one.
entries.reason: No human has ever authored a 3,905-node tree showing what good looks like.

entries.note: The hygiene report writes down mechanical quality criteria: duplicates, restatements, over-length reasons.
entries.reason: Quality is judged subjectively by each reader, so nobody wrote down what good means.

entries.note: Principle clarification separates plugin-provided mechanical quality aids from the interpretation that stays with the user.
entries.reason: The plugin leaves analysis to the user, deferring quality judgment entirely.

entries.note: Tailoring or ranking reasons by reader insight is analysis the user's requirement keeps out of the plugin.
entries.reason: Usefulness depends on whether a reason sparks insight for a particular reader.

entries.note: The 6/10 was a one-off judgment; this tree, catalog and ledger now map its causes to concrete changes.
entries.reason: Ratings like 6/10 were never tied to explicit scoring criteria.

entries.note: The eval suite writes acceptance criteria down as graded checks on shape validity and hygiene report presence.
entries.reason: Rubric writing was not treated as part of plugin development.

entries.note: Tacit quality is articulated by demonstration: agent instructions gain a specific-versus-generic example.
entries.reason: Tacit expertise about good causal reasoning is hard to articulate as rules.

entries.note: The eval avoids reference matching entirely, grading shape and hygiene rather than wording similarity.
entries.reason: Reference-matching scores would penalize valid causes worded differently from the reference.

entries.note: Stdlib token-overlap near-duplicate detection is non-blocking flags only, acknowledging string metrics cannot decide equivalence.
entries.reason: Semantic equivalence between reasons requires judgment that string metrics cannot provide.

entries.note: Embedding similarity would add dependencies or network calls; stdlib token overlap is used instead.
entries.reason: Embedding similarity thresholds for treating two reasons as the same cause were never calibrated.

entries.note: LLM judging is declined inside the fix loop as flaky and costly; non-blocking hygiene flags substitute.
entries.reason: LLM-as-judge scoring was not explored as an alternative to exact references.

entries.note: Without a reference tree, novel causes are never scored as errors; the eval grades only objective properties.
entries.reason: Novel correct causes absent from a reference would be scored as errors.

entries.note: Author's past inexperience with open-ended evals; the actionable part is IMP-18.
entries.reason: The author lacked experience designing evaluations for open-ended generation tasks.

entries.note: Hand-authoring an expert gold-standard tree is recruiting and dataset-building work outside the plugin.
entries.reason: Hand-building a gold-standard 3,905-reason tree would take experts many hours per problem.

entries.note: The smoke preset yields a 3x3 tree of 39 reasons that one person can review carefully.
entries.reason: Each full tree contains thousands of reasons, far beyond what one person can write carefully.

entries.note: Exponential growth is controllable once init --breadth/--depth make shape a stored parameter.
entries.reason: The five-per-level structure grows exponentially with each added level.

entries.note: Human attention limits are outside plugin control; smaller presets exist separately under IMP-02.
entries.reason: Human attention degrades sharply after writing a few hundred related statements.

entries.note: A human tree-authoring tool serves reference-dataset building, which is out of scope for a generation-only plugin.
entries.reason: No tooling exists to help humans author deep trees incrementally.

entries.note: Partial checks become cheap via smoke preset and plan --only for selected branches.
entries.reason: Partial reference trees were not considered as a cheaper substitute.

entries.note: Sourcing domain experts to author depth-5 reasons is a social remedy, not a plugin change.
entries.reason: Depth-5 reasons require domain knowledge few individuals possess across all branches.

entries.note: Hiring or recruiting domain experts is an organizational remedy outside the plugin.
entries.reason: Domain experts needed for credible causes are expensive and unavailable to a solo plugin author.

entries.note: Budget for paid reviewers is a recruiting concern the catalog declines as out of scope.
entries.reason: The plugin is a personal project with no budget for paid reviewers.

entries.note: Assembling multi-domain expert reviewers is social work, not a plugin artifact.
entries.reason: Problems span software, organizations, and processes, requiring several kinds of expertise.

entries.note: The plugin is released: published at github.com/JoshuaRamirez/five-whys and listed in the RedJay marketplace.
entries.reason: Experts have little incentive to donate time to an unreleased prototype.

entries.note: Building a user community to crowdsource reference trees is an organizational remedy.
entries.reason: No user community exists yet to crowdsource reference trees.

entries.note: Recruiting and briefing reviewers is explicitly out-of-scope social work.
entries.reason: Recruiting and briefing reviewers is coordination work nobody planned.

entries.note: Automated hygiene flags take over the mechanical part of reviewing generated trees.
entries.reason: Certifying generated trees as known-good by review also takes enormous time.

entries.note: The show subcommand now prints any subtree with its ancestor chain, so links are checkable in place.
entries.reason: Verifying each causal link requires reading the reason's entire ancestor chain.

entries.note: Cross-branch exact and near-duplicate detection is automated in hygiene.json at assemble time.
entries.reason: Detecting repeats across 25 branches needs cross-comparison of thousands of reasons.

entries.note: An accept/reject review interface is a viewer-style heavy infrastructure the catalog declines.
entries.reason: No review interface exists to mark reasons as accepted, rejected, or duplicate.

entries.note: index.md of levels 1-2 and branch-by-branch paging let the roughly 128k-token output be read in parts.
entries.reason: The roughly 150k-token output is too large to review in one sitting.

entries.note: A reviewer rubric only matters for recruited certification reviewers, which is declined as social work.
entries.reason: Reviewers would need a rubric that does not yet exist.

entries.note: A multi-domain benchmark of expert trees is public dataset building, declined as out of scope.
entries.reason: A meaningful benchmark needs many problems across domains, multiplying the authoring effort.

entries.note: Eval cases at smoke size can cover several problem statements to check generalization of shape and hygiene.
entries.reason: One tree cannot reveal whether quality generalizes to other problem types.

entries.note: Defining a problem taxonomy for a benchmark is dataset research, not a plugin change.
entries.reason: Selecting representative problems requires a taxonomy nobody has defined.

entries.note: Per-domain expert authoring or validation is recruiting work outside the plugin.
entries.reason: Each new domain requires fresh expertise to author or validate its tree.

entries.note: Statistically powered quality benchmarks require large dataset building, declined as out of scope.
entries.reason: Statistical confidence in scores needs many samples, not a handful.

entries.note: Eval grades shape validity and hygiene presence, which survive prompt wording changes with little maintenance.
entries.reason: Benchmark maintenance grows whenever plugin prompts or structure change.

entries.note: A design-independent eval grading shape and hygiene is cheap to keep as the design changes.
entries.reason: The effort could not be amortized because the plugin design might still change.

entries.note: Shape stored in run.json lets evals and checks read it rather than fixed-shape references.
entries.reason: The hard-coded 5x5 shape may become configurable, invalidating fixed-shape references.

entries.note: Eval criteria do not depend on prompt wording, so evolving prompts do not obsolete them.
entries.reason: Prompt wording is still evolving, so early benchmarks risk measuring an obsolete design.

entries.note: Version number reflects past maturity; no artifact change follows from the label itself.
entries.reason: Version 0.1.0 signals the design is not stable enough to freeze.

entries.note: README gains a design decisions section recording what is permanent: stdlib-only, generation-only, complete trees.
entries.reason: No decision records commit to which parts of the design are permanent.

entries.note: Shape-parameterized plan, check and assemble remove literal-shape assumptions that would need rewriting.
entries.reason: References tied to shape rather than causal content would need rewriting on each change.

entries.note: Past prioritization of pipeline over evals; the actionable part is covered by IMP-11 and IMP-18.
entries.reason: The author prioritized shipping a working pipeline over creating evaluation assets.

entries.note: Past time spent on fan-out mechanics; those mechanics now work and evals are planned separately.
entries.reason: Getting fan-out and assembly mechanics working consumed the available development time.

entries.note: Orchestration works: a full 26-agent run completed, and the 20-subagent cap fix is committed.
entries.reason: Coordinating 26 parallel sub-agents required debugging orchestration issues first.

entries.note: Fragment validation and assembly exist and produced the assembled 3,905-reason tree.
entries.reason: Fragment validation and assembly had to exist before any output could be evaluated.

entries.note: Past learning curve on packaging conventions; the plugin is packaged and published.
entries.reason: Plugin packaging conventions took time to learn and apply.

entries.note: Past output-format redesign; the one-reason-per-line format is settled.
entries.reason: Token and context limits forced repeated redesign of the output format.

entries.note: Past time-boxing choice; quality work is now captured by IMP codes in this catalog.
entries.reason: Work was time-boxed around a prototype milestone rather than a quality milestone.

entries.note: Treating evaluation as part of building is realized by adding an evals/ case for claude plugin eval.
entries.reason: Prototype culture treats evaluation as a later phase rather than part of building.

entries.note: Rapid-iteration norms rewarding visible features are ecosystem culture outside plugin control.
entries.reason: Rapid iteration norms reward visible features over invisible measurement infrastructure.

entries.note: The plugin is public on GitHub and in the RedJay marketplace, so external users can demand quality evidence.
entries.reason: Personal tools lack external stakeholders who demand quality evidence.

entries.note: Past perception that evals feel unproductive; actionable part is IMP-18.
entries.reason: Evaluation work produces nothing demo-able, making it feel unproductive.

entries.note: Premise overstates: there are no unit tests either; IMP-18 adds an output eval alongside IMP-11.
entries.reason: Habits from traditional software favor unit tests over output-quality evals.

entries.note: Plugin project templates lacking an evals directory is an ecosystem tooling fact.
entries.reason: Plugin project templates do not include an evals directory by default.

entries.note: A full real run completed on 2026-09-13, producing this 3,905-reason tree.
entries.reason: Without a full real run, there was no output to build a benchmark around.

entries.note: init --model lets runs use cheaper models instead of default-model pricing.
entries.reason: A full run is expensive in tokens at default-model pricing.

entries.note: Dispatch waves bounded by the concurrency cap limit simultaneous agents and rate-limit exposure.
entries.reason: Launching 26 concurrent agents risked rate limits the author wanted to avoid during development.

entries.note: Small development shapes become a supported smoke preset rather than ad hoc edits.
entries.reason: Development testing used small shapes or dry runs instead of full trees.

entries.note: The plugin's own 6/10 rating served as a representative problem for a full run.
entries.reason: The author lacked a representative problem worth spending a full run on.

entries.note: This tree, catalog and ledger are kept in docs/self-improvement as retained run artifacts.
entries.reason: Run artifacts were not planned to be kept as future eval inputs.

entries.note: README will state what validation does and does not cover, so a structural OK is not read as quality.
entries.reason: Passing shape validation gave a false sense that output was acceptable.

entries.note: check stays structural, but assemble adds a hygiene report flagging content problems.
entries.reason: The check command prints OK for structurally valid JSON regardless of content.

entries.note: Developer psychology around green checks; no artifact change beyond IMP-06 and IMP-14.
entries.reason: Green checks satisfy the developer's need for closure on each task.

entries.note: The eval makes hygiene report presence an explicit graded acceptance criterion.
entries.reason: Content-quality checks were never listed as acceptance criteria.

entries.note: Mechanical checks are allowed aids; judging meaning is explicitly left with the user.
entries.reason: Structure is easy to verify automatically while meaning is not.

entries.note: Hygiene flags surface duplicates and restatements that glance-level plausibility hides.
entries.reason: Early fragments looked plausible at a glance, discouraging deeper scrutiny.

entries.note: Claude Code provides claude plugin eval, which IMP-18 targets.
entries.reason: Claude Code plugins offer no built-in evaluation framework nudging authors toward benchmarks.

entries.note: Scaffolding tools' output is controlled by Claude Code tooling, not this plugin.
entries.reason: Plugin scaffolding tools generate agents and skills but not eval suites.

entries.note: Recency of plugin eval documentation is an ecosystem fact.
entries.reason: Documentation on plugin evals is newer than typical authoring guides.

entries.note: Marketplace publication requirements are set outside the plugin.
entries.reason: Marketplace publication requires no quality evidence from authors.

entries.note: Scarcity of example plugins with evals is an ecosystem fact.
entries.reason: Example plugins with evals are too scarce to copy from.

entries.note: Immaturity of agent-output evaluation is industry-wide.
entries.reason: Evaluating agent output remains an immature practice across the ecosystem.

entries.note: Absence of a public expert Five Whys dataset is an ecosystem fact outside plugin control.
entries.reason: No public dataset of expert-authored Five Whys trees exists to borrow from.

entries.note: Confidentiality of corporate RCAs is outside the plugin's control.
entries.reason: Real root cause analyses are usually confidential incident reports inside companies.

entries.note: Organizations withholding sensitive postmortem details is an industry fact.
entries.reason: Postmortems contain security, customer, and legal details organizations will not disclose.

entries.note: Narrative style of public postmortems is industry practice.
entries.reason: Public postmortems describe narratives rather than structured why-trees.

entries.note: Legal discouragement of publishing root causes is outside plugin control.
entries.reason: Legal teams discourage publishing admissions of root causes.

entries.note: Proprietary RCA tool formats belong to other vendors.
entries.reason: Internal RCA tools store analyses in proprietary formats.

entries.note: Causal chains staying inside incident teams is organizational culture.
entries.reason: Detailed causal chains stay within the team that experienced the incident.

entries.note: Academic benchmark framing is a research-community fact.
entries.reason: Academic NLP research has not framed Five Whys generation as a benchmark task.

entries.note: Existing causal datasets' focus on short pairs is set by researchers.
entries.reason: Causal reasoning datasets focus on short commonsense pairs rather than deep trees.

entries.note: Perception of Five Whys as management technique is field culture.
entries.reason: Five Whys is seen as a management technique rather than a research problem.

entries.note: Lack of accepted metrics for open-ended causal trees is a research-field gap.
entries.reason: Open-ended causal trees lack accepted metrics researchers could publish against.

entries.note: Research funding priorities are outside plugin control.
entries.reason: Funding favors general reasoning benchmarks over niche methodology tasks.

entries.note: Annotation costs deterring dataset creators is an ecosystem economics fact.
entries.reason: Annotation costs for deep trees deter dataset creators.

entries.note: Published Five Whys examples being shallow chains is a fact about external literature.
entries.reason: Published Five Whys examples are shallow single chains unsuitable as 5x5 references.

entries.note: Textbook Toyota examples are external material the plugin cannot change.
entries.reason: Textbook examples like the Toyota welding robot show one linear chain.

entries.note: Training-material simplification is external teaching practice.
entries.reason: Training materials simplify examples for teaching rather than completeness.

entries.note: Practitioners converting branching analyses to fishbone diagrams is industry practice.
entries.reason: Branching analyses are typically converted into fishbone diagrams instead.

entries.note: Authors stopping at the first actionable cause is external practice.
entries.reason: Authors stop at the first actionable root cause rather than enumerating alternatives.

entries.note: Invented blog illustrations are external content quality.
entries.reason: Blog examples are often invented illustrations rather than validated analyses.

entries.note: Sourcing and adapting adjacent datasets into a benchmark is dataset building, declined as out of scope.
entries.reason: The author did not search for or adapt adjacent causal or fault-tree datasets.

entries.note: Past allocation of research time; nothing further actionable beyond declined dataset work.
entries.reason: Research time went into plugin mechanics rather than literature review.

entries.note: Converting fault-tree data into fragment JSON serves benchmark building, which is declined.
entries.reason: Adjacent datasets would require conversion into the fragment JSON format.

entries.note: Past uncertainty about dataset transfer; the benchmark route itself is declined under R-06.
entries.reason: It was unclear whether fault-tree or causal-graph data would transfer to Five Whys.

entries.note: Author background explains past choices; actionable eval work is IMP-18.
entries.reason: The author's background is software development rather than evaluation research.

entries.note: Past plan omitted data sourcing; dataset building remains out of scope.
entries.reason: No data-sourcing task was scoped in the plugin plan.

entries.note: Lack of funding incentive for a public dataset is ecosystem economics.
entries.reason: Nobody benefits enough from a public Five Whys dataset to fund its creation.

entries.note: Consultancies guarding RCA expertise is industry behavior.
entries.reason: Consultancies treat RCA expertise as a proprietary competitive advantage.

entries.note: LLM vendor benchmark priorities are outside plugin control.
entries.reason: LLM vendors prioritize broad benchmarks that influence leaderboard rankings.

entries.note: Quality-management communities' data practices are external.
entries.reason: Quality-management communities rarely produce machine-readable datasets.

entries.note: Recognition norms for open-source dataset curation are ecosystem culture.
entries.reason: Open-source contributors get little recognition for dataset curation.

entries.note: Market demand timing for AI Five Whys trees is an industry fact.
entries.reason: Demand for AI-generated Five Whys trees is too new to justify investment.

entries.note: Hygiene report specifies mechanical metrics: exact and near-duplicates, restatements, over-length reasons.
entries.reason: Nobody decided which quality metrics a benchmark should measure, so its content was never specified.

entries.note: README design decisions will state the exhaustive generation-only purpose, framing breadth over precision explicitly.
entries.reason: The plugin aims for exhaustive breadth, which conflicts with precision-focused quality measures.

entries.note: Trading coverage for per-reason precision implies pruning, declined because complete trees are required.
entries.reason: Generating thousands of reasons values coverage over correctness of each reason.

entries.note: Design decisions will state that exhaustive generation accepts wrong causes for the user to filter rather than missing ones.
entries.reason: The design never stated whether a missed cause or a wrong cause is worse.

entries.note: Measuring recall needs a reference cause set, i.e., benchmark dataset building, declined as out of scope.
entries.reason: Breadth goals make recall measurable only against an unbounded space of causes.

entries.note: Supports leaving judgment of surprising reasons to the user; plugin-side precision filtering is declined.
entries.reason: Users may value surprising reasons that strict precision metrics would reject.

entries.note: README will document intended use and known limitations, including ideation-style exhaustive generation.
entries.reason: The intended use was never defined as ideation versus diagnosis.

entries.note: Only mechanically scorable criteria, distinctness and restatement, become non-blocking hygiene flags.
entries.reason: Candidate criteria like causality, distinctness, and depth are hard to turn into scores.

entries.note: Judging whether a reason truly causes its parent is analysis kept with the user.
entries.reason: Judging whether a reason truly causes its parent requires domain reasoning, not pattern matching.

entries.note: Near-duplicate flags use stdlib token overlap; being non-blocking, an imperfect threshold only annotates.
entries.reason: Distinctness among sibling reasons has no agreed similarity threshold.

entries.note: Rating systemic depth of causes is interpretation, which the plugin leaves to the user.
entries.reason: Systemic depth of a cause lacks any objective scale.

entries.note: A weighted composite quality score is plugin-side ranking, declined; flags stay separate annotations.
entries.reason: Combining several criteria into one score requires weights nobody chose.

entries.note: Automated stdlib hygiene flagging over all reasons runs during assemble.
entries.reason: Scoring thousands of reasons would need automation that has not been built.

entries.note: Instruction rules on distinctness, restatement and length become measurable hygiene flags.
entries.reason: The why-expander instructions state style guidance but no measurable pass criteria.

entries.note: Prose 'concrete and specific' advice gains a specific-versus-generic example and grounding requirements.
entries.reason: Guidance like concrete and specific was written as prose advice for the model.

entries.note: Over-length reasons are flagged in hygiene.json, making the soft 20-word rule measurable.
entries.reason: The roughly 20-word limit is the only quantitative rule, and it is soft.

entries.note: Hygiene report verifies after the fact whether agents followed distinctness and length guidance.
entries.reason: Instruction authors assumed the model would follow guidance without verification.

entries.note: Past view of prompt writing; converting guidance into checks is carried by IMP-06.
entries.reason: Converting instructions into checks was not seen as part of prompt writing.

entries.note: The self-improvement record links observed output defects to catalog changes.
entries.reason: No feedback loop links observed output defects back to new criteria.

entries.note: Skill, agent and README will state what the plugin provides versus the analysis users perform.
entries.reason: Because users do the analysis, the author never defined what a useful tree enables.

entries.note: Mechanical quality aids are reclaimed as plugin responsibility while interpretation stays with users.
entries.reason: Leaving analysis to the user shifted responsibility for quality judgment outward.

entries.note: User research is explicitly listed as an out-of-scope social remedy.
entries.reason: No user research established what decisions people make from the tree.

entries.note: Modeling root-cause selection would make the plugin select causes, which is declined.
entries.reason: Downstream tasks like selecting root causes were never modeled or measured.

entries.note: README documents intended use and design decisions, giving known-good a stated target.
entries.reason: Without a defined use, known-good has no target to be good for.

entries.note: Plugin is now public, so implicit needs get documented in README limitations and design decisions.
entries.reason: The author is the only user, so needs stayed implicit.

entries.note: Repetition becomes quantified by the hygiene report's duplicate and near-duplicate flags.
entries.reason: Suspected failure modes like repetition and depth decay were never quantified to prioritize metrics.

entries.note: Hygiene report's near-duplicate detection measures overlap across siblings and branches, discounting ancestor words.
entries.reason: No script measures semantic overlap between sibling branches.

entries.note: Per-level counts and average words per level recorded in output support cross-level comparison.
entries.reason: Reason quality was never sampled and compared across levels.

entries.note: A full run now provides observed data: 3,905 reasons, one exact duplicate, measured size and tokens.
entries.reason: Suspicions came from reasoning about the design rather than observed data.

entries.note: Run measurement records per-level statistics, bytes, tokens and dispatch attempts in run.json.
entries.reason: No instrumentation logs per-agent output characteristics for later analysis.

entries.note: The first full run completed on 2026-09-13 and its measurements are recorded in catalog facts.
entries.reason: Quantifying failures was deferred until after a first full run.
